aescripts-packer: Reduces project and layer clutter with one click — organizing After Effects assets by customizable packing and folder structures for a maintainable project panel and timeline.
aescripts-origami: Procedurally generates Voronoi, Delaunay, triangle and square meshes from shape paths, masks or layer bounds — automatic animation graphs control fragment rotation, scale, position, opacity and Trim Paths.
Geometric fragments unfold, fold-transition and grow organically in procedural mesh animation
aescripts-paint-link: Creates live PSD connections between After Effects and Photoshop — frame-by-frame painting syncs back to the timeline in real time, with customizable onion skin, per-keyframe file management and team workflow.
aescripts-paragraph-on-a-path: Auto-orients each line of a paragraph along a motion path — toggle or reverse the path, animate alignment and leading, scale text lines, and convert selected masks into motion paths.
aescripts-parental-controls: Attaches child layers to the actual path, shape or text content of a parent layer — with horizontal and vertical constraints, children auto-reposition when parent size, path or source text changes.
aescripts-parenter: Groups and repositions multiple layers with temporary Parenter nulls without changing existing animation — toggling links, adding/removing children, copy-pasting parent relationships and 3D nulls.
aescripts-parrot: Dynamically links a master layer's motion, effects, masks, shapes and layer styles to many target layers — named markers trigger different actions with adjustable time offsets, then edit only the source animation.
aescripts-paravent: Builds controllable screen-style fold and unfold animation from selected project items — direction, panel count, fold falloff and falloff order adjustable.
Layers are cut into continuous panels that fold and unfold in sequence like a folding screen or accordion
aescripts-pathlink: Transfers vector designs bidirectionally between Illustrator and After Effects — preserving editable paths, layer/group structure, colors, compound paths, gradients, text, clipping masks and some effects.
aescripts-path-visualizer: Draws text, shape or mask path vertices, Bezier curves and handles as animatable graphics updating live with the original path — customizable vertex shapes, line width, colors and handle styles.
Paths presented as technical drawings, blueprints or vector editor UIs with vertices and Bezier handles
aescripts-penpal-2: 40+ vector path editing functions inside After Effects — flip or split paths, align and distribute nodes, pixel snapping, reverse direction, clear tangents and simplify excess nodes, with local-coordinate viewing and editing.
aescripts-paste-multiple-keyframes-2: Smart-copies and pastes keyframes from multiple layers at once — rebuilding relative timing from the current time with loop pasting, optionally preserving easing, temporal/spatial interpolation and keyframe colors.
aescripts-path-me: Collects single or multiple footage paths from the Project panel, timeline or Render Queue in one click and copies them to clipboard or file — also importing footage directly from received Mac or Windows paths.
aescripts-photolapse: Quickly arranges many photos into a Flash Cut slideshow animation — live preview and speed/order adjustment before finishing, with Position-lapse, Rotation-lapse and Scale-lapse controlling the whole group's motion.
Photos flash-cut in rapid rhythm with particle-like position, rotation or scale variations
aescripts-photoorientationfixer: Reads camera photos' XMP orientation metadata and auto-rotates selected layers in a composition — fixing portrait/landscape photos that After Effects does not display in shooting orientation.
aescripts-pinna: Creates freely addable/removable control, follow or track nulls for selected path points — points and nulls follow each other's angles, null animation bakes back into paths, and group-transform offset issues are fixed.
aescripts-pixel-pusher: Nudges selected layers by custom pixel values on X, Y, Z axes — recursive multi-layer operation, keyframes, sub-pixel offsets, multiplier keys and configurable hotkeys for precise layout and animation position tweaks.
aescripts-pixel-melt: Assigns speed and stretch by pixel-luminance curve so every pixel stretches and shifts independently along a chosen direction — other layers can drive speed and stretch, with scanline modulation, coloring, wrapping and gap filling.
The image melts into elongated pixel strips as if dragged by gravity, also forming split scanlines and tear glitches
aescripts-pixelfan: Uses another layer as a stroke texture along any path or mask, with animatable parameters — Original Frame mode directly takes the underlying frame as the unfolded material along the path.
Custom images or animated layers unfold into textured strokes flowing along curves
aescripts-pixelsworld: Runs Processing-style, Lua, GLSL and Shadertoy code in After Effects to generate 2D/3D graphics — building models with a geometry spreadsheet, reading image/audio data and sharing code presets; officially Windows only.
Abstract patterns, 3D geometry, fractals, oceans, clouds and audio-reactive visuals generated live from code and shaders
aescripts-pixelocybe: Dynamically changes mosaic block size and displacement by the luminance of the source or a second input layer — per-RGB, alpha or luminance channels, shaped by curve, phase, shadow, offset and opacity thresholds.
The frame is pulled, misaligned and channel-split by luminance-driven blocks — psychedelic mosaic and digital glitch
aescripts-pixy-halftone: Converts images to square, circle, triangle, diamond, maze or random-pattern halftones by luminance in real time — shape size, spacing, color, size and opacity contrast controls, with source color and alpha support.
The image becomes retro pixel-game or comic-print style geometric dots, with separable light, dark and midtone layers
aescripts-plotter: Turns video or images into vector art with 16 algorithms — blocks, Delaunay, halftone, line art, mosaic, stitches, spirals, stippling and waves — with source colors, SVG export or shape-layer conversion.
Live footage or animation redrawn as animatable line art, stippling, triangle meshes, spirals and plotter-style vector works
aescripts-pointers: Snaps and links any layer or spatial property to another layer's position — auto-handling 2D, 3D and existing-parent coordinate transforms; animatable delay and offset, separate rotation/scale linking, and lights, cameras or effect control points following layers.
aescripts-pop-captions: One-click word-by-word pop subtitle animation from text layers — one control layer manages everything, auto-setting animation range by word count, syncing foreground/background font sizes, and separately controlling text, background color and background animation.
Words pop out one by one on keyframes while the background color block changes in sync
aescripts-position-matte-2: Builds region mattes quickly from World Position Passes exported by 3D software — fewer extra matte channels and manual roto; footage, shapes or precomps as projection, with tiling, offset, world rotation, grid, radial wave and light modes.
aescripts-power-sphere: Generates deformable 3D spheres directly in After Effects — elliptical distortion, spherical unfold and inversion, material sliding, reflection maps, depth compositing, self-shadowing, depth of field, and composition lights and cameras.
Expandable spheres with real shading, reflection and depth — animating from full sphere to flattened plane
aescripts-power-hyperboloid: Generates two-sheet 3D hyperboloids — moved, deformed, inverted, repeated, extended or unfolded to a plane in comp space, with rich shading, self-shadowing, reflections, depth of field and composition lights/cameras.
Two-sheet hyperboloids extend, flip and unfold like horn-shaped geometry with dimensional reflections, shadows and depth
aescripts-power-droste: Creates versatile spiral and Droste recursive transformations — Levels and Strands rendering modes, 3D rotation and unfolding, and separate materials and extra deformation for multiple spiral strands.
The image recursively spirals into the center as a tunnel, or splits into multiple material-bearing arms rotating and unfolding in 3D
aescripts-praymitive: Builds and combines 14 ray-marched 3D primitives in real time on the GPU in After Effects — smooth unions, subtraction, intersection, independent materials and animatable deformation like waves, ripples, twist and bend.
Abstract 3D geometry with smoothly fused materials, specular and rim light, plus twisted, bent and rippled procedural forms
aescripts-precomp-anchor-repo: Repositions anchors or positions by the actual content bounds of layers, compositions or parents — analyzing precomps, masks, Track Mattes and some expressions to cut visual guesswork.
aescripts-prism-2: Auto-assigns label colors by parenting hierarchy, layer or item type, or name prefixes — cycling or grouping colors for masks and Project panel items, making large projects easier to read.
aescripts-pro-io: Links system folders as synced Watch Bins — auto-importing new footage and image sequences; custom naming, destinations and output modules send multiple compositions to AE Render Queue or Media Encoder at once.
aescripts-pseudo-effect-maker-3: Creates Pseudo Effect control panels with custom names, defaults and groups via drag-and-drop — preserving existing expressions and keyframes when updating the control structure, for clean templates and character rig UIs.
aescripts-property-effector: Links multiple effects and properties to a unified Effector Driver — one set of keyframes drives complex animation; cross-composition control, positive/negative direction limits and stacked effectors, no expression writing.
aescripts-project-notes: Keeps text notes and small code snippets in the After Effects workspace — saving to project XMP or external XML, cloud sharing; advanced commands run AE scripts, system commands or apply expressions to selected properties.
aescripts-ps-shape-to-ae-shape: Converts Photoshop Shape Layers or vector masks in imported PSDs into fully editable After Effects Shape Layers — optionally keeping, hiding or deleting the original layers.
aescripts-pt-effectsearch-3: Scans effects used across the entire AE project — locating missing or third-party plugins and the layers using specific effects; results batch-toggle, delete, export, and same-type effects can link as copies driven by a single instance.
aescripts-pt-autoexpress: Applies common Wiggle, Smooth and Loop expressions to selected properties as buttons — loop, ping-pong, smooth, wiggle and X/Y-axis limiting controls for quick procedural animation without writing code.
aescripts-pt-cropprecomps: Crops precomp bounds by the actual image content inside nested compositions — keeping specified margins and handling selected precomps; ideal for shrinking bounding boxes and unnecessary render areas after PSD layer-group imports.
aescripts-pt-importsubtitles: Imports SubRip SRT, WebVTT or Encore Text Script subtitles into AE — generating renderable text with optional background boxes per Character/Paragraph settings, usable in subtitle automation via Dynamic Link or OpenSesame Server.
aescripts-ps-text-converter-for-after-ef: Converts Photoshop text layers into editable AE text, syncing source Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point and mask animation — also fixing anomalous scaling from the built-in conversion and normalizing to 100%.
aescripts-pt-expressedit-2: Searches expressions across the whole project and nested precomps — centralized extract, modify, apply, disable or remove; tests broken expressions, re-enables after repair, and saves common snippets as reusable presets.
aescripts-pt-textedit-2: Searches, replaces and batch-edits text layers and styles across projects — locating missing fonts, handling nested compositions and all text keyframes, and building reusable style presets for font, size, color, leading and more.
aescripts-pt-framerestorer-2: Detects and replaces missing, corrupted or duplicate frames with dynamic interpolation, and inserts frames to fix judder after frame-rate conversion — plus auto-tracking repair, stabilization ghost cleanup, flicker reduction and clone sources for spot removal.
aescripts-pt-layermarkers: Adds markers at selected layers' In, Out or middle points — to the selected layers, a new Solid or a nested composition — for J/K cut navigation; also batch-slices layers by markers with stacking-direction control.
aescripts-pt-contactsheet: Reads markers on footage or precomp layers and auto-arranges the specified frames into single- or multi-page contact sheets/storyboards — scale, composition size, alignment and spacing controls with annotation areas.
aescripts-pt-opensesame: Exports AE projects or specified properties as human-readable text, CSV/TSV data — non-AE users batch-edit text, footage, properties and Render Queue in spreadsheets; also creates project versions backward-compatible with earlier AE releases.
aescripts-pt-opensesame-server: Receives text/CSV variables via JSON API or watched folders — auto-generating template versions and rendering on demand; multi-machine processing, Render Engine/farm delivery, priorities, remote cancellation, logging, error recovery and notifications.
aescripts-pt-ssakaraokeanimator: Imports SSA/ASS and KaraFun KFN subtitles with word/syllable timing — quick basic presets or AE Animation Presets produce wipe, fade, color-change karaoke animation, with bouncing balls and text crawling supported.
aescripts-pt-panorama: Splits panoramic images into multi-sided 3D cylinders by view angle in a precomp — a surround environment for 3D camera moves; side count and overlap control, avoiding seams on fast moves and Motion Blur.
A flat panorama wraps into a multi-sided surround around the camera, pannable and pushable in 3D comps while staying immersive
aescripts-pubes: Generates any number of Shape Layer splines inside a Bezier polygon or along its contour — uniform, random, semi-random or angle-directed distribution, regenerating rotation, color, width and length.
Dense bristle, radial, streamline or contour-following procedural line textures — all splines can aim at a target
aescripts-quadratefx: Generates Treemap-style vector rectangle tiling — random recursive cuts, or subdivision driven by source-layer luminance with RGB sampling; count, direction, size randomness, color and dynamic text controls.
Geometric mosaics, infographic tree maps, luminance-rebuilt block collages, and HUD/data-viz backgrounds
aescripts-pt-shiftlayers: Shifts selected layers by a fixed time in batch, or staggers each layer by frames/seconds in selection order — aligning the first In or last Out to the current time, ordering from CTI or accumulating offsets on original times.
aescripts-queue-work-area: Adds the current composition to the Render Queue with a custom In/Out from the Work Area — changing the work area and adding again renders multiple segments of the same comp in one go; panel and headless modes.
aescripts-queueup: Saves output folders and Preview vs Final Render/Output Module templates per job — one-click apply and queue after selecting a comp; Final auto-places into a finals subfolder, reducing delivery setup errors across projects.
aescripts-quick-menu-3: Keyboard-invoked floating search box — finding and running effects, plugins, AE menu commands, scripts, Extensions, Shape Filters, Animation Presets and expression templates; recents, favorites, custom groups and auto-created Expression Controls.
aescripts-quickdraw: Auto-creates and organizes End keyframes for every Stroke of Paint Effects — time allocation by stroke length, even spacing, overlap, gaps or stagger, plus duplicate-layer or effects-stacked Track Mattes.
Hand-drawn lines, signatures or traced text write out stroke by stroke in actual drawing order, paced automatically by line length
aescripts-quickflip: Illustrator/Photoshop-style buttons for quick horizontal/vertical flips, clockwise/counterclockwise rotation, scale and opacity steps — modifier keys force new keyframes or batch-modify all existing keyframes on the properties.
aescripts-quick-lens-flare: Builds AE-native Lens Flare/Optical Flares rigs driven by 3D nulls or lights, with optional foreground occluder layers — flares position easily in imported or tracked camera scenes and are naturally occluded by objects.
Lens flares pinned to 3D world positions move with the camera and are naturally hidden behind foreground objects
aescripts-quickportals: Places customizable Portal templates into live-action shots using AE's 3D Camera Tracker — Neon, Sigil and Pixel main styles with multiple duration/look presets.
Neon rings, magic sigils or pixelated portals appear in tracked live-action space, with the shot traveling through the gate into another scene
aescripts-quickscript: Pastes, edits and runs ExtendScript directly inside Adobe apps — auto-indent, JavaScript Linter and output Console; AE-specific features search command names/IDs and fetch property paths.
aescripts-random-layer-selector: Randomly picks layers from the current selection or the whole composition — Most, Many, Not Many and Very Few sampling densities for batch-applying effects, labels or operations to irregular subsets.
aescripts-randomatic-2: Creates static Random, animated Random or Wiggle for large numbers of 2D, 3D and color properties without writing expressions — single-axis, increments, sync, intensity, loops and multiple easings; also randomizes layer Offset, Stretch and order.
Mechanical jumps or organic drift, plus controllable random palettes from two-color gradients, up to ten-color palettes or HSL ranges
aescripts-rapid-reel-composer: Auto-splits long footage into short clips by marker In/Out pairs or a fixed-length Lazy mode — auto markers, stagger/overlap ordering, cross-layer marker and comp transfer, batch precomp, Time Stretch, volume and fade tools.
aescripts-randsomator: Converts text character by character into ransom-note layout — random font mixes from system typefaces, per-character or global rotation, scale, offset and styles; procedural paper texture included, with manual per-character replacement.
Ransom-note/magazine-collage headlines from mixed fonts, sizes and paper snippets with controlled irregularity
aescripts-rapid-slideshow-presentation-m: Builds expression-driven Slideshows, presentations or Reels from image folders — batch photo scheduling, pan/zoom and Push motion, grid/Bento layouts, borders and blurred backgrounds, audio allocation and crossfades.
Single-photo pushes, dynamic multi-frame Bento layouts, 3D camera moves and Swing/Flash transitions form a rhythmically consistent photo show
aescripts-real-ease: Adds intermediate control points between two selected keyframes — smooth animation via acceleration, peak speed and deceleration physics; adjust Peak, insert constant-speed segments, apply easing presets, copy-paste animation curves.
aescripts-recursive-mosaic: Cuts an image into a grid, then recursively subdivides blocks by a detail threshold — mosaic strength, initial grid count, recursion depth, sampling curves and phase; other layers drive strength, with separate RGB/Alpha channel handling.
Adaptive pixel blocks of varying sizes that preserve key outlines, plus JPEG-compression fragmentation and RGB-phase color blocking
aescripts-remove-unnecessary-mask-keyfra: Analyzes AE Mask Tracker's per-frame mask paths — first removing keyframes too similar to the previous frame by vertex-displacement threshold, then a Reinforcement Pass restores intermediate keyframes where change was too large, balancing simplicity and contour error.
aescripts-renamer2: Batch-renames compositions with drag-and-drop naming blocks — fixed text, resolution, duration, aspect ratio, project name, frame rate, date and custom menus combined; live preview, plus preset save/import/export.
aescripts-render-frame-at-markers: Adds the frames at all Layer or Comp Markers within the work area to the AE Render Queue — batch Save Frame As → File — for review stills, thumbnails or marked key frames in one pass.
aescripts-renderq: Four customizable buttons pre-bound to Render Settings, Output Modules and output locations — batch-queueing selected or current compositions; video, stills, thumbnails, multiple output modules and combined outputs, auto-stripping frame/timecode suffixes from still filenames.
aescripts-repeater: Repeats any AE layer in real time into a controllable 2D array of any count and direction — no text-to-Shape conversion or precomp; offset rows/columns separately, set direction by angle, mirror copies, and adjust per-copy time offsets and stagger order.
Still-editable text, shapes, solids, footage or 3D layers extend into regular grids, diagonal patterns or time-staggered repeated animation
aescripts-retrack-2: Integrates AE tracking data — rebuilding missing/off-screen tracks from Mask, Tracker Point, Mocha, Face Track, Transform or 3D Camera data, with a virtual edit layer for quick fixes over original per-frame keyframes; exports Mask, Corner Pin, Transform, 2D/3D Null and more.
aescripts-responsive-tools: Makes text and layers auto-fit content or composition size — Comp, Layer, Target and Size text-adaptation modes, nine-point Anchor Point locking, and layer pinning to the eight composition edges/corners; no extra layers, no breaking existing animation.
aescripts-repositionanchorpoint: Quickly places selected layers' Anchor Points at the nine common bounds positions, compensating Position to keep actual placement in the comp viewport; multi-layer batch processing and split-dimension position properties supported.
aescripts-reveal-in-finder: Reveals the corresponding footage files directly in macOS Finder or Windows Explorer from various AE contexts — including the composition timeline; bindable to AE keyboard shortcuts, or runnable as KBar JSX/JSXBIN buttons.
aescripts-reverse-text: Batch-reverses the content and direction of selected text layers — handling Arabic, Hebrew and other RTL languages on AE versions with incomplete Bi-directional Text support; recognizes numbers, special characters and mixed LTR segments, with paragraph, multi-layer, keyframe and RTL animation-direction fixes.
aescripts-review-importer: Brings review comments from Frame.io, Vimeo, Kollaborate.tv or Screenlight.tv CSV exports directly into AE comps — the script builds text layers and markers at comment timecodes with optional label colors; toggling layers shows feedback on-screen without bouncing to a browser.
aescripts-roop: One-click seamless-looping random 3D space from selected layers — Space, Floor, Ceiling and left/right wall loop structures, with auto camera, background, vignette, virtual surfaces and reflections; random layer placement with target-area avoidance, plus a viewpoint tool for quick camera moves.
3D tunnels and space loops where the camera keeps traveling and objects spawn infinitely around — also immersive scenes with floor reflections, ceilings or walls
aescripts-roll-it: Analyzes Bezier Shape or Mask contour edges and builds a rolling rig so complex or compound shapes roll precisely over their own outline with layer Rotation — Shape, Mask or both; Bodymovin/Lottie output compatible.
Irregular icons, glyph outlines, wheels or whole masked layers undulate and flip along their contact edge rather than sliding on a fixed radius like circles
aescripts-save-objects-2: Saves compositions, single or multiple layers, property presets, masks, markers, keyframe interpolations, expressions, JSX and fonts into a searchable, previewable cross-project asset library — nested folders, multi-comp batch save, shared source paths, Collect Files/font collection and backups.
aescripts-reversemaskpath: Reverses the travel direction of selected mask paths without moving vertices or tangents — fixing stroke, path animation and direction-dependent calculations.
aescripts-rubikcube: Creates and animates rotatable Rubik's Cubes in After Effects — skipping the tedious manual arrangement of small cubes and per-layer rotation setup.
A dimensional Rubik's cube made of many small cubes, twistable layer by layer
aescripts-scene-clip: Catalogs scenes in a composition with thumbnails and annotations for one-click jumps — export/import lists for team collaboration and handoffs.
aescripts-screen-mapper: Designs multi-screen, video-wall or Bento Grid layouts on a standalone canvas, then auto-builds correctly named, colored and positioned AE master comps and precomps — grids, gutters, rulers, snapping and layout sharing.
Multiple differently-proportioned display areas precisely tile into video walls, stage LED walls or Bento split screens
aescripts-screen-saver-exporter: One-click packaging of After Effects or Premiere Pro videos into distributable screensavers or Windows .scr files, with fill and fit playback modes.
aescripts-scribe: Generates shape-layer text from a built-in single-line font library that preserves per-character writing animation — adjustable writing progress and stroke thickness, plus reordered strokes, modified glyphs, and Repeater or gradient shape operations.
Text writes out or erases stroke by stroke along single-line paths like a pen tip, keeping natural handwriting stroke feel
aescripts-search-and-select-properties: Searches AE properties in a composition by name and selects multiple results at once — Strict mode for exact matches, copy/paste of selected properties, cutting the time spent expanding complex layer groups.
aescripts-select-every-other-layer: Selects and deselects layers quickly with free ranges, specified intervals or up/down directions — every-other, every-Nth and progressively shrinking selections, with keyboard shortcuts and instant result feedback.
aescripts-select-layers-pro: Selects layers quickly by type, state, label color or count patterns with buttons — handles unlock, Solo, Shy, and copies selection states so the same group can be recalled after layer reordering or additions.
aescripts-sequencelayers: Batch-staggers selected layers' In points starting from the current comp time in selection order — turning a stack of layers into a timed sequence in seconds.
aescripts-set-matte-texture-packs-01-02: High-resolution looping texture assets made for animation — 12 unique frames per material, quickly joined into loops, in multiple resolutions and formats including 8K and 16-bit EXR options.
Hand-scanned textures subtly shift in short loops, adding natural paper and grain variation to flat graphics, text or backgrounds
aescripts-set-parent-to-structure: Auto-creates layer parenting links according to the Duik character rig structure — skipping repeated per-layer Parent assignment, with one-click unlink; officially supports Duik 17.
aescripts-set-path-keyframes: Adds keyframes at the current time for all Path properties of selected Shape Layers via the Animation menu or custom keyboard shortcuts; removes them when the time already has full keyframes.
aescripts-set-render-queue-time-span: Batch-modifies Render Queue items' start and end times — per-item composition work area, full comp duration or custom start/end frames, applied to all or only checked items.
aescripts-shaketracker2ae: Imports Apple Shake tracking data into After Effects as null objects — reusing existing tracked motion on AE layers and comp elements.
aescripts-shape-layer-toolbar: Adds Shape Layer components and Expression Controls quickly with customizable buttons — saving values, expressions, expression-hidden original values, gradients and keyframes per component, plus one-click selection of same-type components.
aescripts-shape-library: One-click creation of basic Shape Layers — rectangles, circles, stars, hearts, arrows, clouds and more — and storing your own logos, icons, single paths or entire shape layers in a renameable, cross-computer custom library.
aescripts-shape-motion: Creates circular, rectangular, polygonal, heart, starburst or looping motion for layer positions or any multi-value property — control nulls adjust radius, speed, sides, easing, start/end points, rotation and scale.
Objects orbit along regular geometric outlines, and multi-dimensional properties cycle through the same path periodically
aescripts-shape-repeater-baker: Bakes every copy produced by a Shape Layer Repeater into independently controllable shape instances — optionally removing the original Repeater afterwards, for per-copy edits, animation or splitting.
aescripts-shapemonkey: Generates procedural Shape Layer animation at scale with modular shapes, interpolation combos, palettes, radial arrays, transitions, drift and turbulence — using your own shapes, text and vectors, with marker-triggered beat sync.
Many geometric shapes unfold, drift, recolor and transition by arrays, palettes and time markers — continuously changing abstract motion design
aescripts-sheetah-spritesheet-tools: Renders an entire AE comp into a single Sprite Sheet quickly — auto-estimating row/column layout with alpha preserved, exporting PNG, TGA, TIF and power-of-two sizes; also custom frame playback order with text or JSON animation-sequence export.
All frames of a frame-by-frame animation align neatly in a transparent atlas for 2D/3D game engines to play in order
aescripts-shortcakes: Auto-scales and arranges selected layers in a composition into a split screen by specified X/Y counts — different footage and comp sizes supported, with borders, numbering and shapes, exported as PNG.
Multiple videos or photos scale proportionally into a tidy grid with dividers and numbering — multicam comparison, portfolio or info walls
aescripts-signal: Rebuilds analog TV transmission via luminance/chrominance modulation, encoding and decoding — degrading signal segments separately with multiple noise types, VHS tape texture and TV curvature, not just a vintage overlay.
Realistic VHS look with chroma bleed, signal jitter, bottom switching noise, curved scanning and soft bright edges
aescripts-simple-text: Animates text position, anchor, rotation, scale and opacity with familiar Shape Layer controls, then applies the motion to any text layer — regular, reverse or random delays between characters, words or lines, refined with Bezier paths and the Graph Editor.
Text enters staggered character-, word- or line-wise along custom paths, with forward, reverse or random timing
aescripts-simplifymasks: Analyzes selected masks and removes vertices that least affect the outline — preserving shape with fewer nodes; ideal for tidying the dense, jittery paths from AE Auto-trace.
Jagged, node-dense mask outlines become smooth and easy to adjust while roughly keeping the original boundary
aescripts-skin-retouch: One-click Photoshop-style frequency separation in AE — splitting high-frequency detail (pores) from low-frequency color/tone; blur only the low band for smoothing, or use Clone Stamp on the detail layer to remove wrinkles.
Skin color and shading become smooth and even while pores, fine hairs and skin texture remain — no plastic-face look
aescripts-skinanchor: Moves layer anchors to left/center/right and top/middle/bottom intersections with a nine-grid button pad — Shift-click moves the layer instead while keeping the anchor; Alt-click changes the panel skin.
aescripts-skydome: One-click 3D environment background comp that responds to camera position, orientation, rotation and lens settings — drop any HDRI or other image into the background comp as the scene environment.
HDRI skies and surrounding backgrounds keep consistent spatial orientation and perspective as the camera rotates or changes focal length
aescripts-slabtext: Auto-fits each line of a paragraph to the same available width — horizontal scale or Tracking fills the line width, with leading adjustment, auto color and format preservation, plus one-click conversion removal.
Lines of varying lengths all stretch to the same width, forming the tight blocky Slab Typography common in posters
aescripts-slackout: Draft/Final output buttons apply a specified preset to AE comps, auto-increment filenames and render next to the project or to custom folders — uploading straight to Slack channels or users when done, with optional local-file deletion.
aescripts-slate-create: Builds intro clapperboards for selected comps quickly — auto-filling data from the comp name, generating correct info by comp size, aspect, frame rate and length; three templates swappable with your own art, saveable field layouts, for reviews, version deliveries and team shot identification.
A tidy production info board appears before the video, listing project, shot, version, date, resolution and frame rate fields, brandable
aescripts-slctr: Selects layers before, after or at the current time indicator — limited by layer type, label color and work area; also moves relative timing together to the playhead, or flips layer order, for re-arranging complex comps when music changes.
aescripts-slice-it-3d: Cuts precomp layers into multiple simulated-3D-depth parts along 2D masks — six cut modes, adjustable color, shadows, deformation, lights and thickness; shared or per-part materials, thickness auto-syncing to mask position with keyframable animation.
Flat images slice open like cardboard, cubes or hollow shells with customizable textures on the cut faces — fragments separate, twist and reassemble in 3D space
aescripts-smart-adapt: Batch-creates screen and social size versions from one or more master comps — scaling by width or height, per-size alignment, auto-picking the closest aspect-ratio master to duplicate and adapt; size lists support groups, prefixes/suffixes, save and import/export (monthly and yearly pages are the same tool).
aescripts-smart-key-reverse-2: One-click reversal of complex multi-layer keyframe animation while preserving relative timing, interpolation and Roving Keyframe behavior — reversing across playhead, work area or each layer's In to Out, limited to all, selected or specific properties, e.g. turning fades into symmetric fades quickly.
aescripts-smart-keyframe-navigator: Two bindable-hotkey scripts jump precisely to the previous or next keyframe: checking the whole timeline when nothing is selected, only selected layers, or only between selected properties — solving default J/K limits in complex timelines.
aescripts-smart-posterizer: Scans real visual changes in precomps, shapes, images or video — other keyframed properties only update when the source changes frame; closer to frame-by-frame animation rhythm than fixed-rate Posterize Time, with 2s/3s/4s presets and result baking. The experimental feature also makes textures follow rendered objects with squash & stretch.

builtin-ae-colorama: Maps luminance onto a custom color wheel, for psychedelic color shifts, thermal imaging, energy, or metallic colors.
The image mapped into psychedelic or heat-vision colors
builtin-ae-black-white: Monochrome conversion with per-color luminance control, giving more depth than plain desaturation.
builtin-ae-cc-toner: Multi-point tone mapping that assigns colors to shadows/midtones/highlights separately, for split toning.
Shadows and highlights carrying different tints
builtin-ae-keylight: The strongest built-in green-screen keyer (by The Foundry), handling hair and semi-transparent edges cleanly; the first choice among free options.
The green screen cleanly removed, leaving only the subject
builtin-ae-linear-color-key: Linear color keying with progressive removal by color similarity, often used as a cleanup pass after Keylight.
builtin-ae-advanced-spill-suppressor: Removes green/blue spill reflected on the subject, keeping skin and hair free of color fringes.
Green reflections on the subject's edges disappearing
builtin-ae-key-cleaner: Cleans edges and noise after keying, repairing compression artifacts and ragged alpha.
Keyed edges becoming clean and solid
builtin-ae-set-matte: Uses another layer's channel as this layer's matte, sharing a matte without a track matte.
The layer being revealed/cut by another image
builtin-ae-drop-shadow: Basic drop shadow with adjustable distance, angle, and softness, for lifting text and graphics off the background.
An offset shadow behind the object
builtin-ae-radial-shadow: Point-light shadow that radiates and distorts with the light position, more spatial than Drop Shadow.
A shadow radiating from the light source
builtin-ae-bevel-alpha: Adds bevel and lighting to alpha edges for raised 3D edges, commonly used on text and buttons.
Edges with a chamfered, dimensional look
builtin-ae-cc-sphere: Wraps the image onto a 3D sphere with rotation and lighting; most commonly used for planets and crystal balls.
The image wrapped on a rotating sphere
builtin-ae-cc-cylinder: Wraps the image onto a 3D cylinder with rotation and lighting, for cans, columns, and scrolls.
The image rolled onto a rotatable cylinder
builtin-ae-cc-spotlight: Spotlight illumination with adjustable cone angle and soft edge to light a local area.
A local area lit by a cone of light
builtin-ae-add-grain: Adds film grain with per-film-type presets for size and strength, giving digital footage a filmic feel.
Fine dynamic grain surfacing over the image
builtin-ae-match-grain: Analyzes a reference footage's grain and applies it to the target layer, matching CG or keyed elements to live action.
Grain identical to the reference footage
builtin-ae-remove-grain: Noise reduction with per-channel control, suited for rescuing high-ISO noisy shadows.
Noise disappearing and the image turning clean
builtin-ae-noise: Adds noise, optionally affecting color only, for rough textures or breaking up overly clean gradients (banding).
The image covered in fine speckles
builtin-ae-median: Median filter that smooths detail while keeping edges; removes noise or gives a painterly, plastic look.
Detail smoothed while edges stay sharp
builtin-ae-echo: Stacks frames from multiple points in time for afterimages, trails, time repeats, and light-path accumulation.
builtin-ae-posterize-time: Reduces the frame rate for stop-motion, stepped, or retro stutter looks.
Motion becoming choppy frame by frame
builtin-ae-time-displacement: Uses a grayscale map to decide which time sample each pixel pulls, for time warps, slice scans, and surreal effects.
Different regions of the frame showing different moments
builtin-ae-timewarp: Built-in optical-flow retiming for slow motion and frame interpolation; not as good as Twixtor but free.
builtin-ae-3d-camera-tracker: Built-in 3D camera solve: analyzes live footage to recover camera motion and a 3D point cloud, letting you pin text/3D elements into the scene.
3D elements firmly locked into live footage
builtin-ae-warp-stabilizer-vfx: Built-in stabilization that automatically analyzes and removes handheld shake; VFX mode can stabilize without cropping for later tracking.
builtin-ae-card-wipe: Slices the frame into cards that flip over into the next shot, with control over flip axis and order.
Square cards flipping over one by one to reveal the next frame
builtin-ae-gradient-wipe: Dissolves in an order driven by another layer's luma; the most versatile custom transition — any black-and-white image makes any wipe shape.
The frame dissolving along a grayscale pattern
builtin-ae-linear-radial-wipe: Linear or radial wipe transition with adjustable angle and feather; the most basic reveal/switch method.
A boundary sweeping across the frame
builtin-ae-cc-glass-wipe: Molten-glass transition where the frame flows away like melting.
The frame flowing away like melting
builtin-ae-cc-light-wipe: Glowing wipe transition whose boundary pushes the frame open with a halo.
A glowing boundary expanding to push the frame away
builtin-ae-cc-twister: Twisting flip transition where the frame twists like a ribbon to reveal its back side.
The frame twisting over to reveal another side
builtin-ae-cc-warpomatic: Distortion dissolve driven by image luminance; two frames interpenetrate and morph into each other.
Two frames morphing and bleeding into each other
builtin-ae-block-dissolve: Random block dissolve with adjustable block size and softness, for a digital feel.
The frame vanishing in random blocks
builtin-ae-cc-hair: Simulates hair, threads, and fibers that sway with motion and wind, for fur, grass, or flowing filaments.
Fine strands naturally bending and swaying
builtin-ae-particle-playground: Controls large particle counts via cannon, grid, and layer-textured sources, for fireworks, swarms, or image-driven particle animation.
Diverse particle crowds driven by layers and force fields
builtin-ae-cc-environment: Wraps the layer into a spherical environment reflection map, adding ambient reflections to pseudo-3D objects like CC Sphere or CC Cylinder.
Spherical environment reflections on object surfaces
builtin-ae-detail-preserving-upscale: Upscales while preserving sharp edges and detail, for upgrading low-res footage to HD or 4K comps.
Sharper edges and fuller detail after upscaling
builtin-ae-brush-strokes: Turns the image into scattered rough paint strokes, for oil painting, hand-drawn, or stippled looks.
builtin-ae-cc-burn-film: Adds film burn, scratches, and damaged edges for old-movie, retro-title, or burnt-film transition looks.
Yellowed, scorched, scratched, and damaged film
builtin-ae-cc-plastic: Builds glossy plastic relief from image luminance, giving text, graphics, or textures an embossed surface.
Glossy plastic relief with mirror highlights
builtin-ae-cc-vignette: Darkens or brightens frame edges to focus attention, for cinematic vignettes, dreamy light edges, or lens focus.
Clear center with edges gradually darkening or brightening
builtin-ae-cc-grid-wipe: Reveals the next frame cell by cell in rows of grid blocks, for checkerboard, pixel-tile, or modular transitions.
A grid of blocks flipping open or vanishing in sequence
builtin-ae-cc-image-wipe: Uses another image or texture as a wipe matte, revealing the next shot by luminance, clouds, or custom patterns.
Reveal advancing along the reference image's luminance and texture
builtin-ae-cc-jaws: Switches frames with two rows of jagged edges closing like jaws, for monster, comic, or playful impact transitions.
Jagged upper and lower edges closing like teeth
builtin-ae-cc-line-sweep: A moving straight line sweeps across to reveal the frame, for crisp title reveals, split screens, or linear switches.
A clean reveal advancing with a straight scan line
builtin-ae-cc-wide-time: Blends frames from before and after into continuous afterimages, for ghost trails, motion paths, or dreamy time blur.
Semi-transparent motion trails layered across frames
builtin-ae-cc-cross-blur: Blurs horizontally and vertically separately, for softening footage, cross highlights, or directional transitions.
Soft blur overlapped horizontally and vertically
builtin-ae-cc-radial-fast-blur: Fast radial blur pulling outward from a chosen center, for high-speed pushes, bursts, or zoom transitions.
Fast radial streaks extending from the center
builtin-ae-cc-composite: Blends the original pre-effect layer back with the result in various blend modes, for detail retention, matte control, or quick pre/post mixing.
Original footage and the effect result recombined by blend mode
builtin-ae-cc-color-neutralizer: Adjusts red/green/blue channels to neutralize or shift overall color casts, for white balance fixes, cast removal, or stylized tones.
Color casts neutralized into balanced natural colors
builtin-ae-cc-color-offset: Offsets the phase and position of RGB channels, for RGB split, psychedelic shifts, or digital glitch fringing.
RGB channels separated, forming colored edges
builtin-ae-cc-bend-it: Bends the layer between two specified endpoints, giving arms, branches, text, or rods flexible pivot motion.
The object bending like a soft rod between two ends
builtin-ae-cc-bender: Bends the layer into a smooth arc along the vertical axis with a single control point, for arched text, curved signs, or soft flags.
The layer forming a continuous smooth arc vertically
builtin-ae-cc-blobbylize: Shapes the layer into soft, gooey liquid or jelly surfaces, for melting text, slime graphics, or organic morphs.
Rounded, swelling jelly- or slime-like soft surfaces
builtin-ae-cc-flo-motion: Builds a smooth grid-flow morph with two pairs of control points, for stretching faces, twisting shapes, or liquid transitions.
The image flowing and stretching smoothly around control points
builtin-ae-cc-griddler: Cuts the layer into an adjustable grid of tiles, for block decomposition, modular collages, or cell-by-cell reveals.
The image split into regularly arranged individual squares
builtin-ae-cc-smear: Drags and stretches local pixels between two points, for elongating objects, speed trails, or manual liquify.
Local image stretched like wet paint
builtin-ae-cc-split-2: Splits the layer in two along an adjustable angle and moves the halves apart, for split screens, bidirectional reveals, or clean divider transitions.
The frame split into two sides along a soft line
builtin-ae-cc-tiler: Tiles the layer across the whole comp, for seamless backgrounds, repeating logo walls, or animatable tile patterns.
The same image repeating regularly across the full frame
builtin-ae-cc-threads: Generates twisting, flowing threads or fibers, for abstract streams, energy beams, wire, and dynamic backgrounds.
Multiple fine strands interweaving and flowing
builtin-ae-cc-simple-wire-removal: Removes wires or small objects along a line defined by two points, for rigs, cables, and long thin flaws in locked-off shots.
Wire-like distractions naturally covered by surrounding footage
builtin-ae-3d-channel-extract: Extracts auxiliary channels such as depth or normals from 3D image files, for depth-of-field, fog, and layered compositing.
builtin-ae-depth-matte: Builds foreground/background mattes from a 3D depth channel, for isolating objects by distance or spatial layered compositing.
builtin-ae-depth-of-field: Simulates camera depth of field from a depth channel, adding defocus and focus shifts to 3D renders.
builtin-ae-extractor: Extracts specified render channels from multi-channel files like OpenEXR, for separating AOVs, mattes, and light passes.
builtin-ae-fog-3d: Fades distant areas into fog based on the depth channel, adding aerial perspective and depth to 3D renders.
builtin-ae-id-matte: Generates mattes from object or material IDs in 3D files, for adjusting specific models or materials separately.
builtin-ae-identifier: Reads identification channels from RLA/RPF files to select objects or materials, for quickly creating mattes of specific 3D elements.
builtin-ae-backwards: Plays the layer's audio in reverse, for suck-back sounds, reversed speech, and transition preludes.
builtin-ae-bass-treble: Adjusts low and high frequencies separately, for quickly fixing muddy or harsh sound or adding thickness.
builtin-ae-delay: Delays and repeats audio to create echoes, for spatial ambience, rhythmic repeats, and special effects.
builtin-ae-flange-chorus: Short delayed modulation producing flanging or chorus, for thickening vocals, metallic sweeps, and dreamy timbres.
builtin-ae-high-low-pass: High- or low-pass filtering to limit audio frequency bands, for removing rumbling lows, taming highs, or phone-voice effects.
builtin-ae-modulator: Modulates audio to change pitch and timbre, for robotic voices, metallic resonance, and sci-fi sound effects.
builtin-ae-parametric-eq: Precisely adjusts center frequency, bandwidth, and gain, for fixing resonances, boosting speech, or shaping timbre.
builtin-ae-reverb: Simulates room or hall reflections, blending dry recordings into a scene or creating expansive space.
builtin-ae-stereo-mixer: Controls left/right channel volumes and blending, for fixing stereo balance or panning sound.
builtin-ae-tone: Generates a tone at an adjustable frequency and volume, for test tones, electronic beeps, or simple cues.
builtin-ae-bilateral-blur: Smooths same-colored areas while preserving strong edges, for skin softening, noise reduction, and surface smoothing without losing outlines.
builtin-ae-box-blur: Quickly averages pixels with a square sample, for background softening, repeated blur, and performance-friendly transitions.
builtin-ae-sharpen: Increases edge contrast between neighboring pixels for a crisper look, quickly tightening slightly soft footage and graphics.
builtin-ae-smart-blur: Selectively softens areas based on an edge threshold, for skin smoothing, reducing fine noise, or flat cartoon-like blocks.
builtin-ae-unsharp-mask: Fine edge sharpening with radius and threshold control, restoring photographic detail without amplifying overall noise.
builtin-ae-arithmetic: Performs add/subtract/multiply/divide operations on color channels, for technical compositing, channel fixes, and special color processing.
builtin-ae-blend: Blends two layers with ratios and modes, for quick cross-fades, overlays, and simple transitions.
builtin-ae-calculations: Blends specified channels from two layers into a new result, for building alpha mattes and complex channel compositing.
builtin-ae-channel-combiner: Converts between color channel representations such as RGB and HSL, for extracting luminance, swapping channels, and technical grading.
builtin-ae-compound-arithmetic: Performs compound numeric operations between the source and current layers, for difference maps, mattes, and experimental compositing.
builtin-ae-invert: Inverts specified channels such as RGB, luma, or alpha, for negative looks, inverted mattes, and complementary colors.
builtin-ae-minimax: Expands or shrinks specified color channels, for fattening mattes, shrinking edges, filling holes, or removing specks.
builtin-ae-remove-color-matting: Removes fringing from premultiplied background colors, fixing white edges, black edges, and spill around keyed footage.
builtin-ae-set-channels: Assigns each red/green/blue/alpha channel from source layers, for channel swapping, matte combining, and technical grading.
builtin-ae-shift-channels: Replaces output channels with other color or alpha channels, for quickly extracting mattes, rearranging RGB, and monochrome results.
builtin-ae-solid-composite: Composites a specified solid color behind transparent areas, for previewing alpha, adding background colors, or exporting opaque frames.
builtin-ae-auto-color: Automatically analyzes highlights, midtones, and shadows to neutralize casts, for quick fixes of uneven color temperature.
builtin-ae-auto-contrast: Automatically sets black and white points to expand tonal range, for quickly improving hazy, flat, or low-contrast footage.
builtin-ae-auto-levels: Automatically adjusts black/white points and levels per channel, for quick exposure fixes and RGB balancing.
builtin-ae-brightness-contrast: Directly adjusts overall brightness and contrast, for quick light/dark fixes, punch, or softening flat frames.
builtin-ae-broadcast-colors: Limits overly bright or saturated signals to broadcast-safe ranges, for checking and fixing illegal colors before TV delivery.
builtin-ae-change-color: Selects a specific color and adjusts its hue, lightness, and saturation, for recoloring objects or fixing local colors.
builtin-ae-channel-mixer: Remixes the ratios of red/green/blue channels, for cast fixes, custom black-and-white, and special color mapping.
builtin-ae-color-balance: Adjusts RGB balance in shadows, midtones, and highlights separately, for cast fixes or warm/cool split grading.
builtin-ae-color-balance-hls: Controls overall color with hue, lightness, and saturation, for quick recoloring, desaturation, or tonal shifts.
builtin-ae-color-link: Samples an average color from another layer or region and applies it, letting graphics sync their colors with the footage.
builtin-ae-color-stabilizer: Tracks sample points to compensate for frame-to-frame brightness or color changes, stabilizing time-lapses, scans, and flicker.
builtin-ae-equalize: Redistributes luminance or RGB histograms to expand contrast, improving hazy frames and uneven tonal distribution.
builtin-ae-gamma-pedestal-gain: Controls black level, gamma, and gain separately for precise correction of shadows, midtones, and highlights.
builtin-ae-leave-color: Keeps a specified color and desaturates the rest, for selective color, subject emphasis, and color-pop looks.
builtin-ae-levels-individual-controls: Adjusts overall and per-RGB levels with independently animatable controls, for keyframed grading and fine channel correction.
builtin-ae-ps-arbitrary-map: Loads a Photoshop arbitrary map curve to redistribute tones, applying existing curve presets and special inversions.
builtin-ae-selective-color: Adjusts CMYK proportions within red, yellow, green, and other color ranges, for fine-tuning skin, sky, and specific object colors.
builtin-ae-shadow-highlight: Recovers detail in overly dark shadows and bright highlights, fixing backlit, unevenly exposed, and high-contrast footage.
builtin-ae-tint: Maps black and white to two specified colors, for black-and-white, duotone, and brand-color images.
builtin-ae-tritone: Assigns colors to shadows, midtones, and highlights respectively, for tritone posters, vintage, and branded styles.
builtin-ae-4-color-gradient: Generates a smooth multi-color gradient with four movable color points, for dynamic backgrounds, soft lighting, and brand palettes.
builtin-ae-checkerboard: Generates a checkerboard with adjustable size, position, and colors, for geometric backgrounds, grid mattes, and test patterns.
builtin-ae-circle: Generates a circle or ring with adjustable radius, edge, and fill, for ripples, markers, and simple shape animation.
builtin-ae-ellipse: Generates an ellipse with adjustable size, center, and thickness, for outlines, mattes, radar circles, and motion graphics.
builtin-ae-eyedropper-fill: Fills a contiguous region with the color at a sample point, for quickly recoloring line art, icons, and solid areas.
builtin-ae-fill: Fills content with a specified solid color while preserving layer transparency, for quickly recoloring text, icons, and mattes.
builtin-ae-fractal: Generates zoomable mathematical fractal patterns, for abstract backgrounds, psychedelic animation, and infinite-zoom visuals.
builtin-ae-grid: Generates regular grid lines with adjustable spacing, thickness, and color, for tech backgrounds, perspective floors, and composition guides.
builtin-ae-paint-bucket: Spreads fill from a point into similarly colored areas, for coloring closed line-art regions or quickly swapping local color blocks.
builtin-ae-bezier-warp: Bends the whole layer with boundary points and Bezier handles, for conforming to curved surfaces, adjusting packaging art, and soft morphs.
builtin-ae-corner-pin: Maps the layer to any quadrilateral with four corner points, for screen replacements, sign compositing, and perspective correction.
builtin-ae-magnify: Magnifies a local circular or square area, for detail display, tutorial callouts, and magnifying-glass animation.
builtin-ae-offset: Shifts the image with overflow wrapping back from the opposite side, for seamless background scrolling and texture seam checks.
builtin-ae-reshape: Morphs image outlines using source and destination masks, for object shape transitions, face morphing, and morph animation.
builtin-ae-ripple: Generates expanding wave distortion from a center point, for water ripples, shockwaves, and energy pulses.
builtin-ae-spherize: Projects a local area onto a spherical bulge or depression, for crystal balls, fisheye looks, and circular inflation.
builtin-ae-transform: Controls position, scale, rotation, skew, and shutter angle at the effect level, for stacked transforms and motion-blurred transitions.
builtin-ae-twirl: Spins the image around a center into a vortex, for whirlpools, liquid swirls, and twisting transitions.
builtin-ae-warp-stabilizer: Analyzes camera motion and reduces shake through cropping and warping; ideal for stabilizing handheld, walking, and aerial footage.
builtin-ae-cc-block-load: Simulates the image loading in as large pixel blocks, for digital interfaces, low-res looks, and blocky reveal transitions.
builtin-ae-cc-threshold-rgb: Applies a threshold to red, green, and blue channels separately, for color posterization, digital posters, and high-contrast color blocks.
builtin-ae-cc-radial-scale-wipe: Radial wipe that scales from the center or edges to switch frames, for circular bursts, lens zooms, and dynamic reveals.
builtin-ae-cc-scale-wipe: Combines slide and scale to switch between two frames, for quick push/pull, card page turns, and dynamic camera transitions.
builtin-ae-cc-slant: Slants the whole layer along a direction, for tilted text, speed-sense cards, and parallelogram distortion.
builtin-ae-cc-split: Splits the layer from the center and moves the two halves apart, for frame splits, bidirectional reveals, and divider transitions.
builtin-ae-color-range: Selects a range of colors with eyedroppers and creates transparency, for multi-colored backgrounds, green screens, and local keying.
builtin-ae-difference-matte: Compares the frame with a clean background to build a matte, removing static backgrounds in locked-off shots while keeping moving subjects.
builtin-ae-matte-choker: Shrinks, expands, and softens alpha edges in stages, for cleaning up ragged key edges, small holes, and unstable mattes.
builtin-ae-refine-hard-matte: Reduces chatter and trims edges on hard-edged mattes, for products, architecture, and rigid-object keying.
builtin-ae-refine-soft-matte: Preserves hair, motion blur, and semi-transparent detail while refining soft-edged mattes, for complex keys like people and smoke.
builtin-ae-simple-choker: Quickly shrinks or expands matte edges with a single value, for removing white fringes, beefing up alpha, or tweaking key outlines.
builtin-ae-dust-scratches: Smooths isolated dust and scratches by radius and threshold, for restoring old film, scanned photos, and fixing small spots.
builtin-ae-color-difference-key: Uses the color difference between foreground and a specified background color to create transparency, for classic blue/green and high-contrast screens.
builtin-ae-inner-outer-key: Defines definite foreground and background with inner and outer mattes, then computes edge transparency, assisting complex outline keying.
builtin-ae-extract: Creates transparency from luminance histograms and black/white points, for extracting highlights, smoke, flames, or glows on black.
builtin-ae-noise-alpha: Adds noise to the alpha channel only, for grain dissolves, irregular transparent edges, and textured mattes.
builtin-ae-noise-hls-auto: Automatically varies hue, lightness, and saturation noise over time, for quick dynamic film grain and colored flicker.
builtin-ae-noise-hls: Adds controllable noise to hue, lightness, and saturation separately, for colored grain, analog interference, and rough color texture.
builtin-ae-time-difference: Compares pixel differences between the current frame and earlier/later times, for detecting motion, building dynamic mattes, and abstract trails.
builtin-ae-iris-wipe: Reveals the frame inward or outward with an adjustable shape like a camera iris, for vintage outros, focus, and geometric open/close transitions.
builtin-ae-radial-wipe: Swings a wipe edge around a center across the frame, for clocks, pie progress, radar, and fan transitions.
builtin-ae-venetian-blinds: Opens or covers the frame with multiple parallel slats, for blinds, striped reveals, and segmented transitions.
builtin-ae-apply-color-lut: Loads color lookup tables to transform tones, for technical LUTs, cinematic looks, and cross-camera color matching.
builtin-ae-color-profile-converter: Converts between ICC color profiles, for correcting source gamut, simulating output devices, and managing cross-media color.
builtin-ae-grow-bounds: Expands the layer's bounds available to downstream effects, preventing blur, shadows, displacement, and glows from being cut off outside the original size.
builtin-ae-hdr-compander: Compresses or expands high dynamic range values for intermediate processing, preserving highlights and reducing effect overflow in HDR compositing.
builtin-ae-hdr-highlight-compression: Smoothly compresses extremely bright highlights in HDR frames, preserving overexposed detail, controlling output peaks, and tone mapping.
builtin-ae-color-emboss: Creates emboss relief from image edges while keeping original colors, for dimensional textures, stamped patterns, and colored metallic surfaces.
builtin-ae-scatter: Scatters pixels randomly within a range, for diffused soft focus, grainy edges, and slight disintegration.
builtin-ae-threshold: Converts the image to pure black and white by a luminance threshold, for silhouettes, screen prints, high-contrast mattes, and binary animation.
builtin-ae-bevel-edges: Adds bevel highlights and shadows to the layer's opacity edges, giving buttons, cards, and text simple dimensional thickness.
builtin-ae-timecode: Generates timecode on screen with configurable format and start, for review watermarks, edit sync, frame checks, and delivery markers.
builtin-ae-3d-point-control: Provides a 3D coordinate control referenced by expressions, for centrally driving 3D positions, target points, and procedural animation.
builtin-ae-angle-control: Provides an angle parameter that can be keyframed and referenced by expressions, for unified rotation, direction, and fan animation control.
builtin-ae-checkbox-control: Provides an on/off switch for expression logic, for toggling layer states, styles, loops, and conditional animation.
builtin-ae-color-control: Provides a centralized color picker linked by expressions, managing entire graphic, text, and brand animation palettes in one place.
builtin-ae-dropdown-menu-control: Creates a custom-option dropdown judged by expressions, for MOGRT modes, layouts, and state switching.
builtin-ae-layer-control: Lets users pick a layer for expressions to reference from a menu, for reusable rigs, follow targets, and template controls.
builtin-ae-point-control: Provides a visual 2D coordinate point referenced by expressions, for controlling focus, centers, line endpoints, and procedural positions.
builtin-ae-slider-control: Provides a keyframable generic numeric slider, for centrally driving speed, amplitude, scale, and various rig parameters.
builtin-ae-vr-de-noise: Reduces noise in equirectangular 360 footage and handles seams, for cleaning low-light panoramas and immersive video.
builtin-ae-vr-projection: Converts between 360 projection formats like equirectangular and cube, adjusting viewpoint, for panorama compositing and VR output.
builtin-ae-smear: Stretches and smears local pixels along a specified path, for reshaping, elongating objects, speed trails, and liquify animation.
builtin-ae-keylight-1-2: Greenscreen and bluescreen keying with the industry-standard Keylight engine; ideal for refining edges, spill, and semi-transparent details.
builtin-ae-camera-shake-deblur: Reconstructs frames blurred by camera shake using clearer neighboring frames and optical flow; tune blur duration, flow quality, fix strength, and shake sensitivity. Adobe recommends stabilizing with Warp Stabilizer VFX first, then using this effect to reduce residual motion blur.
builtin-ae-smart-mask-interpolation: Creates intermediate keyframes between two adjacent mask-path keyframes, with control over keyframe rate, vertex paths, bend resistance, matching quality, and vertex addition, so masks with very different shapes transition smoothly; opened from Window > Mask Interpolation.
builtin-ae-cc-mr-smoothie: Built-in Cycore effect that remaps colors by image luminance into smooth gradients, creating psychedelic flowing color shifts.
The image smeared into layered flowing color gradients
builtin-ae-time-reverse-keyframes: Reverses the time order of selected keyframes, for quickly playing an animation backward or turning fades and moves into symmetric fade-out/return animation; found in Animation > Keyframe Assistant.
builtin-ae-cryptomatte: Reads Cryptomatte channels from 3D renders (C4D/Blender/Maya, etc.) to precisely isolate individual objects or materials with one click, no manual rotoscoping; essential for 3D compositing and grading.
builtin-ae-proexr-extractor-identifier: Reads multi-channel OpenEXR: EXtractoR extracts any channel (Z-depth, normals, AO, reflections, and other AOV layers), IDentifier builds mattes by object/material ID, for advanced 3D compositing.
builtin-ae-3d-glasses: Built-in: combines left/right eye frames into stereoscopic visuals, outputting red/blue (anaglyph) 3D or side-by-side/interlaced stereo formats.
builtin-ae-rolling-shutter-repair: Built-in: fixes the jelly/rolling-shutter effect (tilted, leaning frames) from fast pans or vibration on CMOS sensors.
builtin-ae-cineon-converter: Built-in: converts between Cineon/DPX film logarithmic (log) and linear color spaces, for scanning film footage.
builtin-ae-vr: Built-in toolkit for 360/VR footage, applying effects directly on the equirectangular projection without seam distortion.
builtin-ae-cc-glue-gun: Draws dimensional lines with sticky globular particles, like a hot-glue gun squeezing out lines; often used for handwriting or slime lettering.
Shiny glue-like lines squeezed out along a path
builtin-ae-cc-overbrights: Flags brightness values beyond the normal range in 32 bpc float projects, checking by RGB, Lightness, or Luminance. Clip mode overlays a custom alert color on the original image to mark overbright pixels; Solid mode extracts them on black, using red/green/blue to show which channel overflowed — pair with Levels or Exposure for precise HDR highlight monitoring. 8/16 bpc projects detect nothing because their value range is fixed.
Overbright areas overlaid with a vivid alert color, or extracted per RGB channel on black, making clipped highlights instantly visible
builtin-ae-cc-ripple-pulse: Spreads expanding ripples from a chosen center, simulating a stone dropping into water or a cork popping up from under the surface. Pulse Level (keyframed) defines the waveform and inward/outward force, Time Span controls wave speed, Amplitude adjusts peak height; especially handy for syncing with audio via expressions. Animated ripples can also be exported as an RGBA bump map for effects like CC Glass.
Concentric waves spreading outward or inward from a point, making the image bulge, dip, and refract like water; can also display as a grayscale bump wave to drive other effects
builtin-ae-cc-hextile: Hexagonal honeycomb pattern generator that tiles the image with hexagons, with a unique 'smear' drag control.

continuum-bcc-grade: Complete three-zone color grading: global hue, saturation, brightness, contrast, Gamma, temperature and RGB first, then the same set applied separately to positionable, range-adjustable shadows, midtones and highlights; Flash can also reduce contrast with a chosen color in darks or lights.
Shadows, skin-toned midtones and highlights each take on different warmth or cast — precise cinematic three-way grading
continuum-bcc-haze: Simulates a photographic UV/Haze filter — absorbs ultraviolet and reduces the excess blue, faded color and lost clarity from atmospheric haze; adjustable de-haze amount and overall temperature suit quick fixes for blue outdoor shots.
The blue-gray haze on distant scenes weakens — mountains and sky look cleaner, shifting from bluish and washed-out back to clarity
continuum-bcc-high-contrast: Simplified Contrast and Amount controls create extremely high-contrast images, mixable with the original — quickly crushes shadows, lifts highlights into hard-tonal photography, strong silhouettes or graphic black-and-white.
Shadows crush to black, highlights brighten, and gray scale collapses into strong tonal blocks — hard, dramatic contrast
continuum-bcc-kelvin: Specifies source and target color temperature in standard Kelvin values, converting tungsten, daylight and other lighting conditions by the difference; protects highlights, compensates brightness loss, and a rotatable, corner-positioned gradient can correct only part of the frame.
Warm 3200K interiors can be corrected to neutral daylight, or daylight dyed tungsten-warm — the cold/warm shift follows photographic color-temperature logic
continuum-bcc-low-contrast: Spreads bright-area light into darker areas, lowering overall contrast while keeping bright parts bright; light amount, spread distance and shadow brightness are adjustable, with a position, range and blur-controlled luminance mask driving the diffusion.
Highlights softly bleed into shadows, black levels lift while bright areas stay bright — a creamy, low-contrast haze
continuum-bcc-polarizer: Simulates a photographic polarizer that darkens and deepens the blue of the sky — a blue-hue mask isolates the sky, with full color correction and overall warm/cool filtering; a direction, angle, size and corner-position adjustable gradient can limit the polarization.
Washed-out skies turn deep and saturated with clearer cloud contrast; the foreground stays natural through the mask and gradient
continuum-bcc-selective-saturation: Adjusts saturation separately for shadows, midtones and highlights by tonal level — each zone has independent Saturation, center position and coverage range; can desaturate only darks, enrich midtones or restrain highlight color.
Saturation separates precisely along tonal levels — keep vivid skin-toned midtones while shadows go near-black-and-white and highlights stay uncontaminated
continuum-bcc-shadows-highlights: Adjusts strength, position and range for shadows and highlights separately — lifts dark areas and pulls back bright ones; suits backlit subjects that are too dark and slightly blown-out bright skies.
Faces in backlit shadow brighten and blown-out skies pull back — detail re-emerges at both ends of the tone range
continuum-bcc-brightness-contrast: Precise brightness and contrast adjustment for the whole image or specified RGB single/pair channels, with an optional Difference mode — basic tonal correction and fixing casts in specific color planes.
The whole frame or a chosen red, green or blue channel is lifted, deepened or given clearer contrast — a single color plane can be corrected alone
continuum-bcc-color-balance: Photographic-style color balance adding or subtracting red, green and blue independently; Photo Positive weights highlights, Photo Negative weights shadows, and Linear acts evenly across all tones.
The red-green-blue ratio is corrected independently — clear highlight or shadow casts can be removed, or an even warm/cool wash applied to everything
continuum-bcc-color-correction: Comprehensive brightness, contrast, hue and saturation adjustments in Legacy, HSI, HSL, HSV, HSP or HSLuma color spaces, with settable output black and white points.
Hue, saturation and contrast across the whole frame are unified, output range is tightened — clean base correction or dramatic tones
continuum-bcc-colorize: Maps luminance, single RGB channels, their inversions or a Pixel Chooser mask to a gradient of up to six colors — animatable multi-tone and false-color tinting.
Grayscale brightness or a chosen channel maps into layered color ramps — duotone to six-tone posterized, false-color imagery
continuum-bcc-correct-selected-color: Eyedropper-specified color with masks built in RGB, HSL, Chroma or Hue space — adjustable range, mix, blur and choke — correcting only the brightness, contrast, hue and saturation of matched colors.
A chosen object's color is recolored, brightened or desaturated while the background and other colors outside the selection stay untouched
continuum-bcc-hsl: Converts RGB into Hue/Saturation/Lightness space, corrects hue, saturation and lightness separately, then converts back — quick overall recoloring and strength adjustment.
Overall hue shifts around the color wheel, colors become intense or faded, and lightness moves independently without touching individual RGB channels
continuum-bcc-invert-solarize: Inverts RGB, RGBA, alpha, any red/green/blue combination, or directly luminance, hue, saturation and lightness; then mixes with the original for negative-to-mid-exposure-reversal looks.
Colors or chosen channels flip into complementary negatives; half-mixed with the original, tones cross over in the midrange — photographic solarize reversal
continuum-bcc-levels-gamma: Adjusts input black/white points, Gamma and output black/white points for RGB, alpha or specified channels; raising the input black point crushes low-light noise to pure black, and rescues gray, low-contrast footage.
Black levels get cleaner and whites open up, with Gamma lifting or deepening midtones; extreme input narrowing also yields steep, posterized tones
continuum-bcc-multitone-mix: Builds a color map from luminance or positive/negative RGB channels, mapping black, white and three adjustable mid-levels to up to five independent colors; each level can also take colors from two other layers or be disabled.
The image splits into up to five tonal bands from dark to light — multi-color printing or gradient posters, with other layers' colors mixed in at chosen levels
continuum-bcc-tritone: Maps luminance or positive/negative RGB channels to three colors for shadows, midtones and highlights, or disables the mid color for a tint; raising Repeats repeats the color map in ping-pong or jump-back modes for extreme solarize effects.
Black, mid and white bands take on a chosen palette — tricolor print look; repeated mapping flips tones back and forth into intense psychedelic exposure reversal
continuum-bcc-atmospheric-glow: Threshold Glow at its core, plus flicker, volumetric light shafts and procedural smoke/fog placeable before or after the glow; alpha-aware glow, independent RGB sizes, many blend modes and random pulse curves.
Highlights bloom softly outward, light shafts pass through drifting fog, brightness breathing smoothly or bursting suddenly — from natural backlit haze to stylized colored stage atmosphere
continuum-bcc-bleach-bypass: Simulates color printing that skips the bleach step, leaving silver and dye in the image — effectively stacking a black-and-white layer over color; Amount, Saturation, Contrast and color temperature are adjustable.
Color is drained but blacks and contours harden — silver-gray, pastel-like low-saturation high-contrast cinema look, common in war films, crime films and grim narratives
continuum-bcc-cross-processing: Simulates developing C41 color negative in E6 reversal chemistry or vice versa; overall Amount plus RGB/monochrome curves control the irregular color cast, contrast and saturation.
Strong but never fully predictable teal, yellow or magenta casts with raised contrast and saturation — the experimental cross-processed film of fashion photography
continuum-bcc-day-for-night: Simulates night from daylight exteriors, reproducing the classic technique of underexposing two to two-and-a-half stops plus a lavender-blue filter; Diffusion, Moonlight, highlight preservation, exposure compensation and full color correction included.
Sunlit scenes darken into blue-purple dusk, softened as if lit by moonlight; highlights can remain as moon surface, window lights or reflections — quick cinematic day-for-night
continuum-bcc-film-glow: Simulates highlight bloom when film frames hit strong light — Threshold selects glowing brightness, with Intensity, Color, Boost, desaturation and independent RGB-channel halo scales; auto border expansion avoids clipping.
White and bright areas spread like emulsion in every direction — soft, tinted cinematic bloom; animating intensity blooms the frame quickly to full white
continuum-bcc-film-grunge: Adds film dust, hair, scratches, stains, specks, gate weave, exposure flicker, vignette and grain in one pass, each group independently adjustable — successor to the old BCC Film Damage.
Clean digital footage becomes a worn print: vertical scratches and hairs jump, dust specks flicker, frames drift side to side with vignetting and coarse grain
continuum-bcc-flashing: Simulates the Flashing technique of applying small uniform exposure to film at various processing stages; photographic filtering lowers shadow or highlight contrast — Negative/Dupe Negative lifts black levels, Print/Master Positive softens whites.
Shadows stop being dead black and highlights stop glaring — overall contrast is gently compressed and can be tinted, like film pre-exposed around processing
continuum-bcc-light-flicker: Adds regular or random brightness flicker to any shot with Smooth, Spiky, Linear waveforms and light-only, dark-only, alternating modes; a curve preview shows per-frame hits, plus RGB-independent intensity and Prism aberration.
The lighting pulses like a failing tube, firelight or a projector — smooth breathing, sharp jumps or fully random; red-green-blue separation can accompany the edges
continuum-bcc-orbs: Generates colored orbs that drift automatically in random directions — count, lit area, depth softness, size/color randomness, speed and motion consistency are controllable; each orb can flicker independently.
Soft-focus circular bokeh slowly floats through the frame, each winking independently — illuminated dust in front of the lens, dreamy bokeh or supernatural energy dots
continuum-bcc-smoke-and-fog: Separate Smoke and Fog systems add automatically evolving haze — color, speed, direction, opacity, scale and complexity per system, with curated Sprites changing the smoke's form.
Smoke rolls and curls across the frame while uniform fog veils the distance and lowers contrast — from natural white mist and stage haze to thick colored magical clouds
continuum-bcc-three-strip: Recreates the Technicolor three-strip process: originally three black-and-white negatives shot simultaneously through red, green and blue filters, recombined in printing; the three strips' strength and smoothing are independently adjustable.
Colors are rich, clean and dramatic with clearly separated reds, greens and blues — the opulent Technicolor of classic musicals, costume films and hand-drawn animation
continuum-bcc-two-strip: Simulates early two-strip Technicolor: two black-and-white frames shot simultaneously through red and green filters and combined into color; red and green versions plus overall correction are viewable and adjustable.
Skin stays fairly natural but greens lean blue-green and sky or blue objects turn cyan — missing full blue information, with a peculiar, charming early hand-colored film feel
continuum-bcc-deinterlace: Motion-mask composites a second field only where combing appears, converting interlaced footage to progressive; can also simulate 3:2 pulldown or convert 29.97i NTSC to 23.976p film rate.
Horizontal combing on moving edges is filled into continuous contours while static detail stays intact; converted to 24p, motion gains a more filmic progressive rhythm
continuum-bcc-color-gradient: Simulates photographic gradient gels — colors or darkens only part of the frame with a smooth transition back to the original; color, opacity, ND Brightness, direction, angle, size and corner positioning are adjustable.
The sky can deepen into blue, orange or another color from the top while the ground keeps its original tone; a corner can also be darkened diagonally with white highlights preserved
continuum-bcc-color-spot: Tints the whole image with a common photographic gel but keeps a movable, scalable, aspect-adjustable central Spot at normal color; Radius, Falloff and Invert control the focus area and inside/outside reversal.
