A soft-edged circular or oval area around the subject keeps its color while the surroundings tint another tone — like a colored spotlight window; inverted, only the center tints
continuum-bcc-colorize-gradient: Maps shadows, midtones and highlights to up to three independently enabled, positioned colors by image luminance, with a direction/angle/size/corner-positioned Grad limiting the tinted region.
Darks, midtones and lights each take a different color — tritone, thermal-image false color or album-cover grading, fading back to the original from one side
continuum-bcc-dual-gradient: Applies two color filters at once — custom or photographic presets — blended by a rotatable, scalable, bandable, corner-pinnable gradient; highlight preservation and exposure compensation included.
The upper and lower halves take different tones meeting softly in the middle — cool blue sky with warm orange ground, or a diagonal two-color cinematic grade
continuum-bcc-gels: Simulates colored gels placed in front of lights by photographers, cinematographers and lighting designers; selectable color and opacity, preserved white highlights, compensated brightness, and a direction/angle/size/corner-pinnable gradient limiting the applied region.
The whole frame looks lit by colored stage or studio light, or color seeps softly from one side only; highlights can stay white even under heavy gels
continuum-bcc-nd-gradient: Darkens a specified part of the frame in F-stop units without changing color balance — commonly balancing too-bright skies against the ground; highlight preservation plus direction, size, angle and corner positioning.
Overexposed or too-bright skies darken naturally toward the ground's brightness with a smooth horizon transition and no color shift — a real ND grad in practice
continuum-bcc-photographic: Builds digital photographic filters from the spectral transmission curves of Kodak Wratten gelatin filters — full Photographic presets plus Color Conversion, Light Balancing and Color Compensating subsets for major and minor color-temperature shifts and specific spectrum compensation.
The frame shows the color response of traditional optical filters in front of the lens — pulls light and medium color temperatures back to balance, or subtly attenuates specific light to fix casts
continuum-bcc-radial-tint: Blends four colors — upper-left, upper-right, lower-right and lower-left — into a positionable, scalable, rotatable, aspect-adjustable radial gradient, with Normal, Tint, Hue, Lighten, Darken blend modes and an optional Spot mask.
Four corner colors blend softly toward the center — dreamy multi-color halos, colored light leaks or quadrant atmosphere tinting; a soft Spot can preserve or confine the center
continuum-bcc-sepia: Warm brown tint with adjustable Amount and Opacity creates a nostalgic photo feel; white highlights can be preserved, exposure compensated, and a direction/angle/size/corner-pinned gradient applies the brown partially or fades it back.
Color or black-and-white footage turns into a yellowed, brownish old-photo atmosphere while highlights can stay clean; the vintage feel can fade in from one side
continuum-bcc-skin-tone: A set of tinting filters designed to enhance skin tone — selectable color and opacity, preserved highlights, compensated brightness, with a rotatable and corner-positionable gradient limiting the retouching area.
Cool, pale or uneven skin tones are softly tinted into healthier warmer skin, white reflections stay natural; the effect can cover only one side or a local area
continuum-bcc-split-tone: Splits shadows, midtones and highlights into three independently tinted groups — each with color, opacity, Position and Range for precise control over the tinted tonal range and boundaries.
The classic look: cool blue in the shadows, warm orange in the highlights with the midtones tuned separately — cinematic cold/warm split; also tritone posters or vintage print styles
continuum-bcc-sunset: Blends three photographic-preset or custom color filters into one gradient controlling the upper, middle and lower thirds of the frame; highlights can be preserved, exposure compensated, with direction, angle, size and corner positioning.
A flat sky turns into purple-red, orange-gold and warm-yellow bands from top to bottom — instant sunset or dusk mood; the gradient can rotate into a diagonal sunset light
continuum-bcc-tint: Tints the entire image with a specified color — optional black-and-white conversion with brightness, contrast and Gamma, then Normal, Tint, Hue, Lighten or Darken modes; a direction/corner-pinned gradient can limit the region.
The frame becomes a consistent brand color, monochrome poster, or black-and-white re-tinted image; a single tone can also fade back to the original color from one side
continuum-bcc-deband: Smooths pixels in detected banding areas caused by low bit-depth, compression or heavy grading, while preserving real detail as much as possible; mainly Strength-based, with Mocha/Pixel Chooser to limit the range.
The ring-like color banding in skies, walls, fog or glows is smoothed back into continuous, gradual transitions while object textures and contours stay relatively sharp
continuum-bcc-deblock: Automatically reduces blocking/macroblock artifacts from heavily compressed footage — cleans low-bitrate streams, old MPEG, repeated transcodes or JPEG-like sources; GPU-accelerated with mask-limited repair areas.
Checkerboard-like compression squares and hard edges in darks, flat areas and fast motion are softened — the frame stops looking like a rough mosaic while content is kept better than full blur
continuum-bcc-broadcast-safe: Soft-knee limits the top comp's RGB, luma and chroma to specified broadcast standards — EBU 103, PAL, NTSC, 0-100% RGB, Rec.601/709 and custom ranges; Zebra or overlay views show the corrected areas.
Over-white highlights, crushed blacks and over-saturated colors are pushed smoothly into legal broadcast range — visually gentler than hard clipping; diagnostics flag out-of-spec pixels
continuum-bcc-dropout-fixer: Repairs frame/field dropouts from brief signal loss when digitizing faulty tape media — specifies the damaged field, start frame, duration and rectangular or horizontal band range, then replaces with the previous field, next field or a solid color.
Sudden horizontal white bands, color streaks or localized field corruption in VHS/Betacam captures are refilled from adjacent frames; softened masks leave no hard repair seams
continuum-bcc-dust-and-scratches: Evaluates and replaces unwanted dust and scratches with neighboring pixels — Radius sets the search range, Threshold controls which density differences count as defects; a Pixel Chooser can limit repairs to damaged areas only.
Isolated white specks, black dots and thin scratch lines on scanned film or old photos are filled from surrounding image; small radii keep texture, oversized radii smooth detail away
continuum-bcc-pixel-fixer: Repairs dead sensor pixels from digital cameras or sensors that stay fixed at the same spot every frame — enables and positions up to ten repair points, each with X/Y size or shared first-point shape, filled with blurred surrounding background.
White hot spots, colored dots or black dead pixels that never move in the video are covered with neighboring texture; elliptical sizes also handle small sensor-dust specks
continuum-bcc-color-paste: Uses the foreground image's luminance as a mask and pastes a specified color onto the background — grayscale logos, text, textures or light/dark animations cover another frame in a single brand color.
The foreground's light-dark contours become a solid-color graphic over the background — bright areas render the most opaque, dark areas fade into the base
continuum-bcc-composite: Composites foreground and background with an embedded or external matte, adjusting matte choke/blur, foreground transformation, color correction, blur, grain and shadows inside one effect, plus edge-only blending controls.
The keyed foreground is positioned, color- and grain-matched, its edges softened separately and blended into the background with a contact shadow — a more complete realistic composite
continuum-bcc-edge-cleaner: Spatial and temporal controls clean keyed edges — targets per-frame shimmer in hair and other details from compressed green screens; adjustable clean radius, temporal smoothing, alpha contrast, strength and edge sensitivity.
Hair strands and clothing contours stop jittering per frame and compression debris disappears — the alpha boundary becomes stable, sharp, yet detailed
continuum-bcc-edge-composite: Auto-generates an edge matte from the existing alpha, recoloring, blurring or adjusting transparency only on the foreground boundary, and blends that ring with the background — removes aliasing and harsh comp seams.
The subject's interior stays clear while only the thin outer ring is tinted closer to the background and softened — hard edges and aliasing blend naturally into the new scene
continuum-bcc-holdout-composite: Builds a luminance matte from fire, explosion or smoke foregrounds without alpha, cuts a black/specified-color holdout in the background, then re-composites the foreground with Add, Screen or Lighten — avoids normal additive brightening or keyed-color edges.
Black-background live-action fire or smoke embeds cleanly into the scene — bright parts keep energy without the backdrop brightening wholesale; Black Clip can crush milky blacks
continuum-bcc-math-composite: Composites two clips with Add, Subtract, Multiply, Screen, Difference, Darken or Lighten math modes, specifying processed channels and blending strength — light overlays, difference comparison and channel-based compositing.
The two layers add, subtract, multiply or take light/dark by numeric relationship — brightened light effects, darkened textures, contrast outlines or difference colors
continuum-bcc-non-additive-mix: Composites by the relative luminance of foreground and background with a Mix percentage rather than adding pixels — recreates the old video switcher's Non-Additive Mix, commonly for layering smoke and fire while controlling blacks.
Bright fireworks or smoke naturally replace corresponding background areas, unlike Add which keeps stacking brightness; Black Clip removes milky haze from impure blacks
continuum-bcc-optical-dissolve: Simulates traditional optical film dissolves with power functions — the incoming shot B's bright areas appear earlier than its darks, unfolding the cut by tone rather than cross-fading the whole frame evenly.
The next shot's highlights emerge from the frame first with shadows catching up later — a soft, film-print-like dissolve with tonal order
continuum-bcc-pixel-chooser: Independently generates or strengthens Alpha/Track Mattes from luminance and channel thresholds, color keys, geometric shapes, linear/radial gradients, AE Masks, mocha-tracked splines, plus Face ML and Depth Map ML selections.
Specific people, face parts, depth layers, colors or brightness regions become trackable black-and-white mattes — reusable for localized effects and foreground/background compositing
continuum-bcc-linear-color-key: Builds alpha from each pixel's difference against a specified Key Color, definable in RGB, HSL, LCH, Chroma or Hue space; refines with per-channel weights, tolerance, softness, Gamma, Choke and region masks.

The chosen background color and similar ranges turn progressively transparent while the foreground survives; LCH tolerance separates lightness and chroma, Mocha/Pixel Chooser isolates areas that must not key
continuum-bcc-linear-luma-key: Builds alpha from luminance or a single RGB channel, keying pixels above, below, near or away from a Threshold; Similarity, Softness, Gamma, Alpha Offset, Choke and colored Gel output are provided.
Black-background light effects keep only their bright parts, white-background line art keeps its darks, or a specific gray range is removed; choosing the highest-contrast channel gives cleaner edges
continuum-bcc-two-way-key: First removes a color range with Key Color and Similarity, then restores mistakenly keyed foreground to opacity using Keep Color with independent tolerance — suited for footage where background and subject share similar colors that ordinary keys would hole out.
Large background areas are keyed out, but clothing, skin or object colors inside the removal range can be rescued — the matte no longer has foreground holes
continuum-bcc-alpha-process: Processes alpha with separable horizontal/vertical blur first, then corrects black/white points and Gamma, and composites with blend modes against the original alpha; a post-blur removes edge artifacts from combined mattes.
Jagged or overly hard transparency edges soften, semi-transparent ranges are re-converged through black/white points, and two alpha relations can blend into more complex mattes
continuum-bcc-chroma-key: Creates a chroma key for blue, green or red-screen footage, adjusting the matte with Density, Balance, Lightness and RGB channel weights — balancing background transparency, semi-transparent foregrounds and shadows.
Studio single-color backgrounds are keyed out and replaced with new footage; subjects stay opaque while glass, gauze or ground shadows retain proper transparency
continuum-bcc-composite-choker: Two choke groups smoothly shrink or expand the alpha edge, blendable, differenced or subtracted from the original alpha — removes keying residue and can generate contours from two matte rings.
The foreground's transparency boundary shrinks inward to remove green edges or expands to restore detail; Difference mode leaves only the thin contour between the two rings
continuum-bcc-make-alpha-key: Builds a new alpha from this or another layer's luminance, RGB, alpha, inverted or Folded channels, refined with levels, Gamma, blur, offset and choke; outputs composite, inverted composite or the matte directly.
The brightness of a chosen channel becomes transparency directly — bright areas stay, dark areas key out or reverse; Alpha Offset fades the whole layer in from fully transparent
continuum-bcc-matte-choker: Processes source alpha with iterable two-stage Blur, Choke and Gray Soften; positive values shrink the opaque region, negative expands it, or choke one side first and compensate problem edges in reverse.
Matte boundaries become more even after repeated fine shrink/expansion passes and stray edges are eaten away; lowering Gray Soften squeezes gray transparency into crisp binary contours
continuum-bcc-matte-cleanup: Sequential black/white threshold correction, Blend softening and Choke shrink/expand on the matte, with Spread and Gain limiting edge decisions — cleans gray semi-transparent dirt and background residue after keying.
Gray holes inside the matte fill solid, background gray specks turn transparent, and green fringes around people shrink while controllable soft transitions remain
continuum-bcc-premult: Specifies and removes the background color premultiplied into semi-transparent pixels, fixing old background-color edges when alpha footage is placed on a different base; common for black or white premultiplied media.
The old black, white or base-colored edges around composited objects, smoke or glows disappear — semi-transparent edges recover clean color on the new background
continuum-bcc-rgb-blend: Blends the source with a Mix Layer's red, green, blue and alpha channels at different ratios, adjusting per-channel brightness, contrast, layer order and blend mode; Mix Back can create transitions.
Different RGB channels of two frames interweave — fix channel ratios or create red-blue separation, dual-exposure chroma; alpha blends separately between the layers
continuum-bcc-defringe: Isolates and removes colored fringing on high-contrast or overexposed edges, such as purple/blue fringes from sensor overload; red, green, blue, cyan, magenta and yellow mats with per-color target hue, range and saturation.
Purple-blue fringes along backlit branches, metal highlights or white contours are pressed back to neutral while the subject's original color and crisp outline survive
continuum-bcc-lens-distortion: Corrects barrel and pincushion distortion — negative pulls corners outward for barrel, positive pushes inward for pincushion; Anamorphic Squeeze, X/Y curvature and a movable center handle asymmetric anamorphic lens deformation.
Architectural lines that bulge outward or bow inward return to straight, anamorphic footage is un-squeezed; reversing also deliberately makes fish-eye or exaggerated wide-angle perspective
continuum-bcc-radial-exposure: Radially brightens or darkens the center or edges of the frame with a positionable circular or oval Spot, using radius, aspect and Falloff for the transition — corrects lens vignetting or guides the eye with light/dark focus.
Lens corner falloff is evenly brightened, or the surroundings softly darken to highlight a central subject; the exposure gradient feathers along an adjustable ellipse
continuum-bcc-wide-angle-lens: Pulls frame corners outward with Distortion for a quick wide or ultra-wide lens perspective and edge stretch; X/Y Correction compensates over-deformation, and borders can be transparent, extended, mirrored or wrapped.
Central subjects stand out more while surrounding space expands outward — an exaggerated ultra-wide view; horizontal and vertical stretch can be rebalanced so people and lines don't over-distort
continuum-bcc-ambient-light: Adds directionless ambient fill light to the whole scene — raises overall brightness without shadows or visible sources; light gels or custom colors, and Beat Reactor can drive brightness from audio.
The frame brightens like evenly scattered on-set fill light — darks are easier to see without spot zones, cast shadows or a clear illumination direction
continuum-bcc-chroma-bands: Generates adjustable rainbow diffraction patterns around light sources, simulating prism dispersion; controls band period, ray density, inner radius, spread, taper, angle, proportion, softness and noise.
One or more rings of rainbow arcs and fine rays open around the light — lens diffraction, CD reflections or a prism splitting white light into a rainbow
continuum-bcc-eye-light: Places a corner-positionable, scalable, rotatable local fill near both eyes of a portrait — independent X/Y softness, brightness, gel and shadow strength; Add or Screen lifts the eye region.
Eye-socket shadows fade and pupils/whites gain life — a soft oval fill matches the eyes' perspective while the rest of the face stays largely unchanged
continuum-bcc-glow-darks: Builds a matte from a specified position/range of dark tones and produces a Glow/Bloom with separable X/Y blur on shadows and dark areas; the glow's hue, temperature and RGB can be corrected independently.
Black lines and shadows emit soft light outward — like inverted neon or glowing dark ink, the opposite of Glow which only blooms highlights
continuum-bcc-glow-edges: Auto-extracts lines and edges from the source and blooms only that Edge Matte with colorable, separable blur Add/Screen glow; can also glow along the alpha boundary, controlling how much light shows from behind objects.
Object contours and internal texture lines are traced into neon light while flat areas stay darker — glowing line art, circuit outlines or energy strokes
continuum-bcc-ice-halos: Simulates halos, moon rings and rare arc networks from high-altitude ice crystals reflecting and refracting light; patterns selectable by sun height, position limited by luminance/color mattes, and image-luminance displacement makes halos wrap around objects.
Pale colored rings appear around the sun or moon, extending into intersecting arcs across the sky; the halo is disturbed by foreground brightness as if hidden behind clouds or objects
continuum-bcc-key-light: Relights existing images with a directional or point key light, adding the illumination direction and local light/dark modeling missing from the shoot — strengthens key-light presence on people, products or scenes in post.
One side of the subject is concentratedly brightened while the other keeps shadow, or light falls off from a specified point — flat lighting gains direction and dimensionality
continuum-bcc-lens-flare: A dedicated Flare Editor combines hot spots, irises, discs, polygons, rainbow rings, star bursts, streaks and radiation lines — twenty components — into flickering, noisy, boundary-triggerable realistic or sci-fi flares.
Core burst next to strong light, ghost flares aligned across the lens, rainbow rings and star bursts — from natural lens artifacts to complex sci-fi energy
continuum-bcc-light: Projects realistic, deformable, corner-pinnable light and shadow using built-in Abstract, window, foliage, snow and material Gobos, or custom images/sequences; Add, Screen or Subtract for lights and shadows.
Walls or people look lit through real occluders — window panes, blinds, foliage — with positionable light patterns and shadows that can bend around objects by source brightness
continuum-bcc-multi-star: Generates multi-point star bursts at highlight positions via a luminance matte — per-star ray count, size, angle, color and Add/Screen strength, with control over light peeking from behind alpha objects.
Jewelry sparkle, streetlights and metal highlights grow neat multi-ray star lines like a star filter on the lens — from four-point twinkles to dense radiating stars
continuum-bcc-overexpose: Simulates overexposure when a film camera stops — Amount, Intensity and Blur control the bloom coverage, strength and softness; Beat Reactor can drive it.
Brightness rushes toward milky white — highlights blow out first and soften detail, like a film frame that over-sat exposure at a stop or a cut-point flash
continuum-bcc-reflector: Simulates silver or gold reflectors adding white or warm gold light to positionable, range-adjustable shadow areas — post-production rescue of dark outdoor faces without forcing actors to stare into a bright bounce.
Shadows on the backlit side of a portrait lift like a bounce board — silver gives neutral white, gold adds warm skin light, without crudely raising highlights
continuum-bcc-streaks: Extends horizontal and vertical streaks of independently set lengths from a positionable, range-adjustable highlight matte, added with Add or Screen in custom colors.
Streetlights, LEDs and metal reflections stretch into thin horizontal or cross light lines — anamorphic, sci-fi interface or intense highlight streaking
continuum-bcc-rays-puffy: Radiates soft, fluffy volumetric light from a chosen luminance/RGB/alpha or Pixel Chooser region toward a specified source point — Detailed/Fat ray switching with length, extension, contraction, holdout radius and multi-color gradients.
Bright windows, text or cloud gaps spread wide soft light — the beams' edges aren't sharp rays but Tyndall columns puffing open in the mist
continuum-bcc-rays-radiant-edges: Extracts image edges from luminance/RGB/alpha or Pixel Chooser first, then radiates colored Detailed/Fat beams from a source point through the contours; smoothing detail, bloom, degraining and ray-length controls included.
Text, people or object contours become light sources with beams trailing outward from the center — logo burst, divine silhouette or energy rays
continuum-bcc-reverse-spotlight: Specifies the lit region and Near Corner directly in the frame; the effect reverse-computes the Light Source, Target and Cone Width — ideal for setting the pool shape first, plus edge lighting, gels and motion tracking.
The user-boxed ellipse or perspective pool maps to a plausible lamp position and cone — the center can brighten, or negative Falloff makes a ring-shaped spotlight
continuum-bcc-spotlight: Sets Light Source and Target with on-screen control points for a realistic spotlight with adjustable height, cone width, intensity, color and center/edge falloff; alpha/channel-based edge brightening also available.
An elliptical or near-circular follow spot shines on the person or product from a chosen direction — brighter center, soft edges; lowering ambient creates classic stage focus
continuum-bcc-center-spot: Blurs the distracting background but keeps a clear central region — movable, scalable center point with adjustable blur; for portraits, products and focused attention.
The central subject stays sharp while the surroundings gradually soften into blur
continuum-bcc-depth-of-field: Controls blur per region with a mask, gradient or input-image brightness, simulating front/mid/back defocus; works with 3D-rendered Z-depth maps.
Foreground, middle and background get different defocus amounts following grayscale depth
continuum-bcc-diffusion: Lowers contrast and creates soft glow around highlights or shadows; built-in textures shape the diffusion or mask, and blend modes plus deformation make many optical soft-focus looks.
Contrast softens and highlights or shadows take on a textured diffusion glow
continuum-bcc-double-fog: Adds fog with a settable depth range along the vanishing point and distance direction first, then a second bloom pass on the image highlights; fog color, amount, brightness, blur and light color are separately controlled.
Distance fogs along the vanishing point while bright areas bloom softly with light
continuum-bcc-fog: Creates a soft fog atmosphere over the whole image with glowing highlights — humid air, dreams, morning mist or low-contrast cinema moods.
The frame is covered in soft fog with highlights gently glowing through it
continuum-bcc-frost: Edge-aware smoothing reduces wrinkles, blemishes and detail while lowering contrast and adding a slight, tintable glow to highlights — softens portraits while keeping main contours.
Skin becomes smooth and wrinkles fade, with highlights carrying a frosty cold glow
continuum-bcc-halo: Independent horizontal and vertical blurs create an adjustable-opacity soft-focus halo with extra light mist on highlights — lowers contrast and softens facial detail at once.
A wide, soft halo spreads around the subject while highlights carry an additional misty glow
continuum-bcc-mist: Adds slight highlight bloom to luminance-mask-selected areas with adjustable blend mode, brightness, horizontal/vertical blur and color — softens detail and lowers contrast.
Bright parts are veiled in fine mist — overall softness without a heavy halo
continuum-bcc-net: Simulates netting (silk stocking) soft focus used in portrait photography — fades facial blemishes while keeping image sharpness; separate horizontal/vertical spread amounts and blend opacity.
Portrait blemishes are softened while features and overall sharpness remain
continuum-bcc-rack-focus: Simulates real lens defocus with out-of-focus highlights forming circular or polygonal bokeh — aperture blades, curvature, angle, brightness, color and softening are controllable.
The frame pulls out of focus and highlights swell into adjustable circular or polygonal bokeh
continuum-bcc-silk: Edge-aware smoothing softens wrinkles, blemishes and fine texture while keeping coarser features like eyes, nose and mouth — a mask can limit the retouch area.
Skin gains a silky texture while important features like eyes, nose and mouth stay sharp
continuum-bcc-split-field: A positionable, rotatable, feathered divider splits the frame — one side stays sharp, the other out of focus; simulates split-field close-up lenses or directional selective depth.
One side of the divider is sharp and the other blurred, with a softly graduated boundary
continuum-bcc-transform: Concentrates Position, Z Position, independent scale, three-axis rotation, Corner Pin, Shear and four-edge Crop in one effect, with multiple resampling filters, edge handling and shutter-adjustable motion blur.
Flat images can be pushed back, flipped, sheared or fit to any quad — quick screen replacement, card fly-ins and perspective layout; fast animation keeps smooth smearing
continuum-bcc-3d-extruded-image-shatter: Shatters the image into true 3D shards with adjustable thickness, scattered, rotated and lit through space; sides can map the original, stretch, crop, or use solid/multi-colors, with AE comp camera and lights support.
The frame breaks into glass, slate or brick shards with visible side thickness — rolling reveals lit edges and specular highlights, heavier than flat-sheet shatter
continuum-bcc-3d-image-shatter: Cuts the source into rectangular, triangular, torn, random or spiral shards scattering in 3D space along burst, acceleration, linear, centrifugal, centripetal or spiral paths; custom shard shapes and gradient-controlled Scatter Wipes supported.
The image breaks like glass, paper or photos — thin shards fly toward and away from the lens, tumbling randomly; playing in reverse re-assembles them into the full frame
continuum-bcc-cube: Maps the source onto a 3D cube — all six faces can share one image or take separate front/back/left/right/up/down layers; XYZ size, pivot, face separation, camera, light and projection controls.
Multiple images are pasted on a rotatable cube's six faces with diffuse, specular highlights and soft shadows — photo carousels, channel branding and flip transitions
continuum-bcc-cylinder: Wraps source media on a rotatable, scalable, unfoldable 3D cylinder surface — wrap proportion, inside/outside faces, back replacement layer, camera perspective, lighting and projection.
Flat images curve into can bodies, column displays or wrap-around screens with highlights and backs visible when rotating; animating Wrap Percentage flattens the cylinder back
continuum-bcc-fast-flipper: Pixel-resampled fast horizontal, vertical or dual-axis flips, or mirrors left-to-right, right-to-left, top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top; Mirror Offset moves the seam and Blend softens it.
The frame flips instantly sideways or upside-down, or keeps one side and mirrors it into symmetry; the seam stays sharp or melts into a soft kaleidoscopic center line
continuum-bcc-page-turn: Builds a 3D paper plane for book or magazine page turns with different media on the two sides; Offset, direction and Flap Radius control curl progress and curvature, with highlights, shadows and motion smear.
The page corner curls up, revealing the paper's back and the next page, crease catching light with a shadow below; full turns auto-complete or stop at any angle manually
continuum-bcc-pan-and-zoom: Documentary-style pan and zoom automation for large stills — loads comp layers or external images, sets A/B framing, then auto-generates forward or reverse animation, holds, Ease and natural exponential zoom.
The camera slowly pushes into a person, pans to details or pulls back to reveal the whole in high-res photos — smooth starts/stops, motion blur and optional vignette, classic Ken Burns
continuum-bcc-sphere: Maps source images onto positionable, rotatable, croppable, partially unfoldable 3D spheres — independent front/back layers, inside/outside faces, camera pivot, motion blur, three lights and projection.
Flat maps, photos or textures wrap into a self-rotating earth or ball with dimensional luster from spotlights, light sweeps and specular highlights
continuum-bcc-sphere-transition: Wraps the image onto a sphere with animatable Perspective — the key difference from regular BCC Sphere; wrap proportion, un-roll restoration, three-axis rotation, front/back faces, lighting and projection complete the transition.
The flat shot rolls into a rotating sphere, pushes toward or away from the viewer, then unrolls into the full frame — globe flip or sphere-wrap transition
continuum-bcc-mosaic: Samples the source into mosaic pixels with adjustable size and aspect — optional blur before pixelation, horizontal/vertical frame alignment, Shift to move the grid or Scramble to randomly shuffle pixel positions.
Detail becomes large blocks — censoring, low-res pixel art or digital glitch; pre-softening gives smooth color blocks, high Scramble scrambles the frame like shuffled shards
continuum-bcc-color-choker: Processes red, green, blue channels separately or locked as a group — input black/white points, two-stage Choke modes and Post Blur compress, posterize and soften color; optional monochrome conversion remaps channels to custom colors.
Colors compress into bold contours, soft smeared blocks or separated RGB screenprint looks; grayscale can be re-tinted into a few high-contrast art colors — it works on color, not key edges
continuum-bcc-colorize-glow: Generates a Glow Map from a single channel — luminance, RGB, alpha, inverted luminance or cartoon/general edges — then colors the bloom with up to six-color gradients; blur, Spread, Threshold, Overdrive adjustable, with standalone glow output or compositing.

Highlights or contours bloom into multi-color neon with color shifting along the gradient by light strength — rainbow halos, electric outlines and dreamy energy; Cartoon Edges looks like glowing illustration line art
continuum-bcc-drop-shadow: Animatable drop shadow for titles or timeline footage — distance, direction, color, strength, softness and Gamma; Source Opacity fades only the source while keeping the shadow, Avoid Clipping lets shadows exceed the layer bounds.
Soft-edged shadows with controlled direction and distance appear behind text, logos or transparent layers — adds lift and depth; the subject can fade out while its shadow remains
continuum-bcc-emboss: Converts the source to solid color and builds directional highlights and shadows along alpha, luminance, RGB channel or Pixel Chooser edges, simulating raised stamping; light direction, strength, pre-blur, light/dark colors and Highlight Balance.
Image detail turns into metal embossing, paper debossing or stone-carved dimensional ridges — light on one side, dark on the other; pre-blur removes fine noise for bolder relief
continuum-bcc-glow-alpha-edges: Generates tight glowing outlines along the source's alpha channel or mask contours, designed for transparent layers and Masks; Width, Softness, Smoothness and color, with standalone glow output, under-the-subject or overlay placement.
Text, logos or keyed objects get a neon halo hugging their outline — not blooming from every highlight like a general Glow; Under keeps contours clean, Over washes soft light onto the subject
continuum-bcc-multi-shadow: Composites three or more independently configurable drop shadows — distance, direction, color, strength, softness, Gamma, noise — onto the source; shadows can derive from luminance, RGB, alpha or their edges, with Master Controls syncing all three.
Text or graphics cast three colored shadows in different directions at once — retro misregistration, RGB split, cartoon ghosts or multi-source lighting; animated noise makes the shadows sparkle
continuum-bcc-reflection: Produces source reflections on a positionable, rotatable, scalable, sheared virtual plane — Position, Orbit and Pan animatable 3D cameras plus AE Comp Camera; reflections auto-align to the object bottom, with softening, fade and flowing ripples.
Mirror-floor reflections with perspective appear below text, products or logos — fading into smooth glassy reflections or gaining automatic ripples like water, viewable from different 3D angles
continuum-bcc-rgb-edges: Detects adjacent-pixel differences per red, green and blue channel, recomposes a colored edge image and applies it back with an Apply Mode; per-channel strength, Threshold and post-blur, with invert, light/dark edge selection and alpha-from-edges.
Object contours split into red, green and blue lines — chromatic edge tracing, colored emboss or electronic scan edges; different Thresholds leave coarse main contours or dense textures per channel
continuum-bcc-rgb-pixelnoise: Randomly picks a Percentage of pixels and adds red, green, blue noise with lockable ratios, or perturbs only luminance while keeping hue; Clipping/Wrap controls overflow, Random Seed and Perturbation decide static or per-frame variation.

The frame is scattered with red-green-blue bad pixels, digital snow or colored sensor noise — unbalanced channel amounts give strong color mottling; Luma Noise keeps black-and-white grain without hue change
continuum-bcc-scatterize: Moves source pixels into a scattered look — Variance and Scatter Percentage control distance and affected ratio; random scatter, bidirectional linear or from-center radial, with center-weighted or Subtle animation-friendlier algorithms.

People, text or frames shatter into fine pixels drifting apart — digital disintegration, teleportation vanish or explosive radial burst; low scatter keeps the subject's shape with sparse specks around it
continuum-bcc-caustics: Simulates light passing through water surfaces refracted and projected onto a surface — wave fields from source layers, auxiliary layers or built-in Fractals, with wave height, projection distance, filament feel, softness and auto-deformation speed.
Bright interlacing water light like a pool bottom drifts with the waves; higher detail or changed sources give plasma fields, smoky particles and radiating geometric light patterns
continuum-bcc-mixed-colors: Generates procedural color noise images — Scale, Rotation and Offset arrange the pattern, Detail controls color-block boundary roughness, Coarseness the block count and size, and Mutation moves the pattern through 3D noise space.
The frame fills with randomly blended color blocks — low Detail looks like liquid camouflage, high Detail shows fine mottled complexity; can blend over the source as colored texture
continuum-bcc-noise-map-2: Layers multiple 3D noise fields into auto-flowing, morphing black-and-white procedural textures — backgrounds, mattes or control sources for other filters; auxiliary layers or comp shapes can modulate displacement, scale, rotation, turbulence and black/white fade.
The frame becomes continuous flowing clouds, liquid marble or complex black-and-white turbulence; modulation sources push local regions through noise space for shape-constrained distortion
continuum-bcc-jitter: Three visualized Jitter curves drive multiple properties simultaneously with Noise Jumps, Random Walk, Smooth Noise and periodic waveforms — position, XYZ rotation, scale, opacity, brightness, color, plus built-in blur, choke, wipe or key insert effects.

Layers shake, scale and rotate irregularly like handheld footage, with exposure, hue or sharpness flicker alongside; three independent curves stack fine tremors, big drift and intermittent jumps into complex glitchiness
continuum-bcc-jitter-basic: A single Jitter curve adds procedural variation to scale, position, XYZ rotation, opacity, brightness or contrast — jump noise, random walk, smooth noise and regular waveforms, with Amount, Frequency, Seed and Frame Offset.
Camera shake, object wobble, size twitch or brightness flicker without per-frame keyframes — a lighter version than the full one, for one rhythm driving common properties
continuum-bcc-looper: Captures a fixed frame range from a specified Start Frame and loops it — each cycle can shift by Increment, with normal, periodic reset, ping-pong or repeat-endpoint playback; normal mode adds Cross Fade or fade-out/in at the seam.
Short actions replay endlessly, ping-pong forward/back, or take slightly later slices each round; crossfading hides visible jumps — breathing, flames, background motion and rhythmic repeats
continuum-bcc-posterize-time: Samples every Frame Separation frames and holds the frame, lowering temporal resolution for strobing or stop-motion; Time Width alternates normal playback with sampled sections, blended via Original, Dissolve or Transparency.
Smooth video becomes low-frame-rate card stops, stop-motion puppetry or beat-like strobes — each pose holds for frames then jumps; smoothly cycling between fluid and sampled motion also possible
continuum-bcc-temporal-blur: Weighted-average blends the current frame with two or more source frames before and after — blur along time, not space; sampling count, interval, time offset, forward/backward/bidirectional and Gaussian or equal weighting.
Moving objects smear into continuous long-exposure trails along their path while static backgrounds stay sharp; Frame Offset can lag or lead the blur behind the subject
continuum-bcc-time-displacement: Uses another layer's luminance or RGB channels as a time displacement map — each pixel fetches its current, past or future frame by map value; Displacement Amount defines the time span, Reference Level sets the neutral gray, frame blending optional.
Different regions of one frame exist at different moments — time slices swept by gray levels, wave-like motion delays or interleaved body poses; it distorts time, not pixel space
continuum-bcc-trails-basic: Stacks multiple historical frames spaced by a specified interval back onto the source — adjustable count, opacity and blur; the source can also be cropped, scaled, positioned and XYZ-rotated for video echoes and basic feedback.
Moving people leave a string of frame-by-frame clones or translucent ghosts behind — dancers and motion trails unfold like multiple exposure; scaling/rotating each layer forms a feedback tunnel
continuum-bcc-atmospheric-glow-dissolve: Auto-animated transition built on cinematic glow — volumetric light shafts, smoke/fog, light flicker, aberration, lens orbs, film grain, colored blur vignette and full grading, each independently controllable; Percent Done also manual.
Two scenes blend amid blooming highlights, smoke and volumetric light — orbs and aberration rise and fall around the cut: dreamy, mysterious or movie-trailer atmosphere
continuum-bcc-blur-dissolve: Auto-enhanced-then-reduced soft-focus lens diffusion hides the dissolve point between two shots; Box, Pyramid or Gaussian blur with independent horizontal/vertical amounts.
The frame blurs out of focus losing detail, swaps to the next shot at the most blurred moment, then returns to sharp
continuum-bcc-camera-shake-dissolve: Auto camera vibration and deformation mask the dissolve between two shots — separate pan, speed, zoom, rotation, randomness and shutter-style motion blur.
The camera shakes violently with motion smear, switching frames at the peak of the tremor
continuum-bcc-channel-blur-dissolve: Auto-raises then lowers blur through the dissolve, with independent red, green, blue and alpha channels plus horizontal/vertical amounts — chromatic-edged soft transitions.
RGB edges separate as the frame blurs, switching to the next shot at maximum softness
continuum-bcc-crash-zoom-dissolve: Fast, violent zoom distortion masks the underlying dissolve — effect strength auto-rises and falls around the transition; music videos, action edits and beat impacts.
The frame slams toward or away from the center, cutting to the next shot amid radial smear
continuum-bcc-cross-zoom-dissolve: The outgoing and incoming shots each zoom rapidly and cross-dissolve; independent zoom amounts, aspect stretch, center points and overlap timing on both sides, plus shutter motion blur.
The previous shot pushes away while the next slams in, the two zooms meeting and overlapping
continuum-bcc-directional-blur-dissolve: Auto-rises and falls directional blur along a chosen angle to hide the dissolve — independent horizontal, vertical and RGBA channel strengths; high-speed pans or whip shots.
The image drags into long directional streaks, swapping shots at the peak of the smear
continuum-bcc-dissolve: Auto-completes a standard cross dissolve between two shots, or manual percentage keyframing; full grading plus ease-in/out and dissolve-length controls included.
The previous shot gradually fades out while the next fades in — a clean, even crossfade
continuum-bcc-film-glow-dissolve: Traditional film bloom auto-strengthens through the transition, peaking to cover the dissolve between shots; threshold, halo radius, desaturation and per-RGB-channel spread ratios.
Bright areas swell into cinematic soft light, switching shots as the bloom nearly whites out
continuum-bcc-film-roll: Scrolls the frame up or down with dust, hair, scratches, stains, gate weave, flicker, vignette, grain and film bloom — damaged-print transitions.
A dirty, scratched film roll scrolls vertically with flicker, weave and bloom, cutting between shots
continuum-bcc-flutter-cut: Strobe-like rapid alternation of outgoing and incoming frames — separate hold lengths per side with solid-color frame inserts; blur, grunge, glitch, X-ray and inversion processing also available.
Two shots flicker-cut rapidly like a broken strobe, with solid flash frames optionally interleaved
continuum-bcc-light-leaks-dissolve: Up to four independently shaped, colored and animated light-leak textures cover the dissolve point; position, rotation, exposure, blur, bloom, flicker and blend mode.
Color leaks wash in from the frame edges or center, naturally swapping shots at the brightness peak
continuum-bcc-linear-wipe: A freely rotatable straight line auto-wipes between two shots — sharp or feathered edge, with three border layers of adjustable thickness, offset, opacity and color.
A line, optionally with colored borders, sweeps across the frame revealing the next shot behind it
continuum-bcc-mosaic-dissolve: Pixelates the dissolve result between the shots into scalable, displaceable, scrambled mosaic blocks, plus YUV channel blur and prism aberration — digital block transitions.
The frame shatters into coarse pixel blocks that reshuffle with colored aberration before forming the next shot
continuum-bcc-multi-star-dissolve: Multi-ray stars from image highlights with intensity auto-rising and falling through the dissolve; star brightness, count, size, angle, color and luminance-mask range.
Highlights burst into many multi-ray stars, dissolving to the next shot at their most dazzling
continuum-bcc-orbs-dissolve: Random drifting colored orbs generated during the dissolve — count, size, color, depth softness, drift speed and per-orb independent flicker; lens-edge water droplets also simulated.
Soft-focus orbs of varying size and color drift past, blinking and masking the shot change
continuum-bcc-prism-dissolve: Prism aberration and colored smear auto-rises and falls with the dissolve — depth, rotation angle, smear offset, three-segment colors and a moving center, acting on incoming, outgoing or both.
The frame splits into rotating rainbow bands and smears, swapping shots at the peak of dispersion
continuum-bcc-rack-focus-dissolve: Real lens defocus and bokeh cover the dissolve point; horizontal/vertical blur, luminance mask, aperture blades, curvature, angle, color and softening.
The frame gradually defocuses, highlights swell into circular or polygonal bokeh, then swaps and refocuses
continuum-bcc-radial-wipe: A positionable, rotatable, aspect-adjustable circular or oval mask reveals the next shot — inside-out or outside-in, with three independent colored border layers.
A circular or oval opening expands from the center or contracts inward, with optional multi-layer colored rims
continuum-bcc-rays-dissolve: Realistic volumetric beams from a fixed or moving source point, intensity and position varying through the dissolve; length, brightness, color, threshold, texture and flicker.
Highlights pull long volumetric shafts, the source moving and swapping shots at its brightest
continuum-bcc-rectangular-wipe: A positionable, rotatable, scalable, corner-radius-adjustable rectangular mask reveals the next shot — animatable from edges-to-center or center-outward, with three border layers of selectable corner styles.
A rectangular window expands or closes to reveal the next shot, its rim styled with sharp, beveled or rounded corners
continuum-bcc-smoke-and-fog-dissolve: Auto-evolving smoke and fog generated together through the dissolve — separate color, speed, direction, density and blend for both, plus smoke pattern choices and prism aberration.
Thick smoke and thin fog surge to cover the frame, the next shot gradually emerging through the mist
continuum-bcc-smoke-wipe: Auto-evolving smoke acts as a dynamic mask wiping in the next shot; smoke pattern choices, drift speed, direction, density, scale, chaos plus mask choke and softness.
A rolling smoke bank sweeps along the chosen direction, its edges gradually revealing the next frame
continuum-bcc-spin-blur-dissolve: Clockwise, counterclockwise or bidirectional rotational blur warps the frame, with optional zoom spiral and prism separation; the rotation center can travel from start to end point.
The frame swirls into colored spiral smears around a moving center, dissolving at the peak of rotation
continuum-bcc-swish-glow: Simulates a rapid camera whip-pan between shots with soft cinematic bloom added during the swing; pan direction, speed, separation timing, blur and dual-layer RGB halos.
The camera whips sideways into a blurred light band, highlights blooming before settling on the next shot
continuum-bcc-swish-prism: Simulates a rapid camera whip-pan between shots with prismatic color splitting and displacement during the swing; pan direction, speed, separation timing, dispersion depth and three-segment colors.
The frame whips sideways and splits into rainbow bands, swapping shots amid the chromatic smear
continuum-bcc-swish-warp: Rapid camera whip-pan completes the shot change, adding lens distortion pulling corners outward and adjustable blur during the swing; direction, speed and two-shot separation timing.
The frame whips sideways with corners stretched by lens distortion, landing on the next shot
continuum-bcc-texture-wipe: A custom texture image's luminance, RGB or alpha channel acts as a dynamic mask wiping the next shot; pre-smoothing, choke/expand and edge blur.
The next shot seeps through the texture's brightness shapes irregularly — like ink, rust or paper dissolving
continuum-bcc-video-glitch-dissolve: Simulates digital video playback errors with glitch intensity peaking at the dissolve point; block corruption, horizontal band displacement, frame shake, RGB separation and luma/saturation flicker combine.
The image suddenly blocks, tears horizontally and splits RGB, cutting shots at the worst of the glitch
continuum-bcc-vignette-wipe: A positionable, rotatable, aspect-adjustable elliptical vignette mask reveals the next shot — feathered edges plus three border layers with independent thickness, softness, offset, opacity and color.
A soft elliptical aperture opens or closes from the center or edges, revealing the next shot
continuum-bcc-blobs-wipe: Random organic transparent blobs grow continuously to reveal the layer beneath — scale, stretch, softness, turbulence, flow and deformation, with gradient/effect-image offset and multi-layer borders.
Random organic blobs spread like liquid or ink, gradually eating the foreground to reveal the next shot
continuum-bcc-checker-wipe: Two adjustable count/direction band sets interleave into checkerboard cells, switchable to union, intersection or stripe combinations; relative angle turns squares into diamonds, with gradient offset, effect images and multi-layer borders.
Checkerboard squares or diamond cells expand in interleaved waves, revealing the next shot cell by cell
continuum-bcc-colorize-glow-dissolve: Glow from selected or inverted luminance/color channels tinted by up to six-color gradients — blur, spread, threshold and overdrive, with full-frame, circular or linear regions pushing inward or outward.
Highlights glow in multi-color gradients spreading in or out, cutting shots in a colorful bloom
continuum-bcc-composite-dissolve: Two mutually blendable Apply Modes rework the classic cross dissolve, with input/output black-white points and Gamma refining the transition midpoint; Overlay/Soft Light enrich, Multiply/Screen/Add make dark-field, bright-field and bloom dissolves.
The two shots blend in overlay, soft-light or brightening modes — mid-point enriched, darkened or blooming
continuum-bcc-criss-cross-wipe: Two independent multi-band sets combine via union, intersection or single-set stripes into a criss-cross grid; count, width, spacing, angle and random deformation per set, plus gradients, effect images, noise textures and three border layers.
Horizontal, vertical or diagonal bands cross into a grid, expanding row by row to reveal the next shot
continuum-bcc-damaged-tv-dissolve: Simulates a CRT losing or distorting signal during the cut — rolling, jagged edges, static noise, horizontal interference, fading, scanlines and chroma separation, with brightness/contrast peaking at the transition midpoint.
The frame rolls, tears and snows like an old TV losing signal, with scanlines and RGB cast before switching
continuum-bcc-grid-wipe: A crossing grid expands from a specified center or contracts inward to erase the frame — rotation, cell count and boundary width, with double-door, radial-circle or rectangular overall profiles and drop shadows.
Dense crossing lattice opens from the center — door-style, circular or rectangular cell-by-cell reveal
continuum-bcc-kaleida-dissolve: Kaleidoscopic deformation strengthens with transition progress, hiding the underlying dissolve at the midpoint then returning to normal; two independent tile sets, wheel/flower/web/multi-star patterns, circular or linear region sweeps.
The frame splits into rotationally symmetric mirrored patterns and star shards, switching shots at peak kaleidoscope
continuum-bcc-lens-blur-dissolve: Lens defocus/rack-focus blur on both shots' highlights, highlights shaped like simulated apertures; circular or 3-16 blade irises, curvature, rotation, bokeh softness, noise and highlight enhancement.
The frame defocuses first, highlights swell into circular or polygonal bokeh, then focuses into the next shot from the blur
continuum-bcc-lens-distortion-wipe: A virtual lens with continuously changing size distorts one layer to complete the reveal — lens center position, size-change speed, and positive/negative Convergence for convex or concave lenses, with optional drop shadow.
A circular lens like a magnifier or glass ball expands/contracts, switching shots amid convex bulge or concave dimple
continuum-bcc-lens-flare-dissolve: A full 3D Lens Flare component animation masks the cross dissolve — light movement, flicker and glimmer control, combining core highlights, radiant beams, haze, polygons, discs, hollow rings and colored halos.
A large cinematic flare crosses the frame — beams, halos and ghosts hiding the cut at the peak of brightness
continuum-bcc-lens-flare-round: A streamlined Lens Flare control set biased to soft round elements masks the dissolve — light moves between two points, flicker, beam and glimmer adjustable, with round discs, hollow halos and brightness/contrast/saturation peaking at the transition midpoint.
Soft round flares and translucent discs slide along the optical axis, dissolving into the next shot in a gentle bloom
continuum-bcc-lens-flare-spiked: A streamlined Lens Flare control set biased to star-spike looks masks the dissolve — movable, flickering flare, pentagon/hexagon ghosts, tapering central bars and a colorful Chroma Fan of dual-prism arcs.
Sharp star bursts and cross bars explode, rainbow prism spikes and polygonal ghosts sweeping across to finish the cut
continuum-bcc-light-wipe: A light source wipes along the edge of an expanding geometric shape — double-door, circular or rectangular profiles, reversable; light color as solid or sampled from source boundary pixels (more visible radiant beams), optional drop shadow.
A bright light edge pushes outward along door seams, rings or rectangles, trailing rays and revealing the next shot
continuum-bcc-multi-stretch-wipe: Radial erase base with an elliptical stretch first reshaping the contour, then three independent Taffy Stretch groups — strength, angle and rotation speed — pulling the mask into irregular, toffee-like sticky shapes.
The circular mask is stretched into rotating ellipses and toffee points by multiple directions, tearing the frame open like sticky liquid
continuum-bcc-multi-stripe-wipe: Multiple bands like horizontal or vertical venetian blinds complete the erase — band count, width, spacing, direction, rotation and softness, with per-stripe position/width randomization, coherent offset and auto deformation.
Rows of horizontal, vertical or diagonal blind slats open in sequence, widths and positions regular or randomly jumping
continuum-bcc-particle-illusion-dissolve: Full Particle Illusion engine inside the dissolve transition — particle opacity auto-fades in and out with progress while the background dissolves between the shots; point, line, ellipse or area emitters and existing particle libraries for smoke, fire, sparks.
Smoke, sparks or glowing particles surge at the midpoint of the cut, then dissipate to reveal the next shot
continuum-bcc-rgb-blur-dissolve: Single or multiple RGB channel blur rises at the transition midpoint to mask the dissolve — separate red, green, blue channels and horizontal/vertical scales, with circular or linear region sweeps; official docs suggest GPU-accelerated BCC+ Channel Blur Dissolve instead.
Red, green and blue contours each smear in different directions into chromatic trails, then converge into the next shot
continuum-bcc-rgb-displacement-dissolve: Animates RGB channel displacement to gradually reveal the next layer — red, green and blue channels offset along XY with adjustable strength, driven by a chosen layer and channel for horizontal and vertical displacement, with blend modes and region sweeps.
The frame is pulled apart by RGB planes and torn by the displacement map, switching shots amid strong chromatic glitch
continuum-bcc-ribbon-wipe: Multiple parallel transparent ribbons thicken progressively to reveal the layer beneath — ribbon count, orientation, softness and position offset, with extra linear gradients changing each region's reveal order.
Neat parallel transparent ribbons widen in sync, wiping the frame in rows like diagonal blinds or fabric strips
continuum-bcc-rings-wipe: Multiple independent concentric ring bands expand from the center or contract from the frame edges to complete the reveal — ring count, center, offset, softness, rings stretchable/rotatable into ellipses, with gradients and drop shadows.
Rings of concentric circles or ellipses ripple outward like radar waves, revealing the next shot in segments
continuum-bcc-ripple-dissolve: Concentric ripples like raindrops or stones on calm water, distortion auto-rising and falling with transition progress; wave radius, amplitude, width, speed, deceleration and decay, with directional, height-aware lighting on the wave crests.
A single center sends out ring after ring of raindrop ripples, the image refracting along light/dark crests before the cut
continuum-bcc-tile-wipe: Cuts the frame into size-adjustable tiles, animating each tile's own scale and rotation to complete the transition; horizontal and vertical scales lockable or separate (squares become rectangles), optional per-tile original-region restriction and drop shadows.
The frame breaks into regular squares, each tile shrinking or growing while rotating — a dynamic mosaic collage transition
continuum-bcc-tritone-dissolve: Auto-strengthens then weakens tritone tinting and Levels/Gamma while the underlying dissolve runs; separate highlight, midtone, shadow colors, duotone switch, black/white points, Gamma, blend modes and midpoint brightness/contrast/saturation.
Both shots compress into three tonal colors of highlights, midtones and shadows — like duotone print or vintage posters — before dissolving
continuum-bcc-vector-blur-dissolve: Derives a vector direction map from a chosen layer and channel, auto-strengthening stylized blur at the transition midpoint — vector type, angle, texture contrast, blur length and map softness produce smoke strands, painterly strokes or melting blends.
The image is dragged into smoke strands, wet strokes or melting streams along local vectors, blending into the next shot at peak flow
continuum-bcc-water-waves-dissolve: Multiple water-wave distortions with randomizable directions and wavelengths mask the dissolve — wave count, amplitude, speed, main direction and directional spread, plus a focusable spotlight and four-direction ambient reflection colors for dimensional water.
The whole frame undulates and refracts like wind-blown water, multi-directional waves and reflections flowing before the dissolve
continuum-bcc-vr-blur: Seam-aware blur designed for 180/360 monoscopic or stereoscopic media — simulates defocus or lens diffusion; horizontal Blur X and vertical Blur Y adjust independently, with edge wrapping correctly handling the panorama seam.
The whole VR field shows continuous soft focus or diffusion with no hard line at the left-right stitch; larger horizontal blur simulates directional smear from fast panning
continuum-bcc-vr-flicker-fixer: Reduces or removes flicker in 360 footage: Frame Analysis corrects shutter/aperture exposure jumps over the full frame or continuous regions; Temporal Smooth RGB/YCC pixel-blends neighboring frames for local flicker from mixed natural light and artificial flashes.
Panoramic exposure no longer jumps frame to frame, and luminance pulsation from local light sources smooths out; YCC mode stabilizes brightness first while keeping the 360 field continuous
continuum-bcc-vr-insert: Places video, titles or logos into monoscopic or stereoscopic VR media with true 360 spatial perspective — positioned by lat/long, distance, three-axis orientation, scale and opacity; composite in-filter or output a remapped insertion layer with alpha.
A flat title or brand graphic sits like a panel fixed in the panoramic scene, holding correct spatial position and perspective as the view turns; can repeat across multiple cube faces
continuum-bcc-vr-reorient: Re-orients monoscopic or stereoscopic panorama media with Pan, Tilt and Roll in true 360 space — supports 180/360 inputs and multiple stereo arrangements; HMD-style preview and cube-face guides check orientation.
Without cropping the equirectangular panorama, side, rear or tilted scenery can turn to face the viewer, and the horizon and starting view direction are corrected
continuum-bcc-vr-sharpen: Seam-aware sharpening designed for 180/360 monoscopic or stereoscopic media — four scales Fine, Small, Medium, Large enhance detail separately; threshold, scale radius, luminance or independent channel processing, with edge wrapping avoiding panorama seams.

Fine textures through larger contours sharpen progressively across the panorama; noise is suppressed by threshold and the left-right boundary stays continuous, no straight line like regular sharpening
continuum-bcc-polar-warp: Wraps the source into a circular polar deformation approximating a flattened sphere — Repeats, inner/outer radii and Wrap modes repeat the image, with Angle Speed and Radius Offset Speed auto-rotating or sucking in / blowing out.
Rectangular frames roll into discs, tunnel mouths or repeating radial patterns, rotating continuously; enabling Swirl twists the outer ring harder than the center into a vortex
continuum-bcc-st-map: Hardware-accelerated remapping of the target footage using ST/UV Map red and green channels as horizontal and vertical sample coordinates — reads timeline layers or loads external EXR/TIFF, with border fill and post-transform.
The frame bends, stretches, liquefies or conforms precisely to a custom coordinate map — restoring 3D/VFX pipeline ST Maps into animatable lens warps
continuum-bcc-bulge: Makes the source look wrapped over a bulging or recessed curved surface — center, Height, Perspective, Radius and Taper; negative Height caves it in, Stretch and angle pull the round bump into an ellipse or squeeze it narrow.
A local area bulges outward like a round magnifier or caves into a bowl; raising Taper sharpens the smooth sphere into a candlestick-like peak with a narrow base
continuum-bcc-curl: Auto-generates and moves multiple curling deformations — Complexity controls curl count, Distortion Amplitude decides tight or smooth, then Curl Size, movement direction, spacing, speed and random seed.
The frame is pulled by multiple moving tendrils, heat streams or soft water currents — curls fine and coiling or large smooth curves flowing across the footage in a set direction
continuum-bcc-turbulence: Feeds multi-layer procedural noise from Noise Map 2 into a displacement map for jelly-like flowing X/Y distortion — noise scale, complexity, feedback, per-layer rotation and displacement, animated with Flow Rate or Morph Rate.
The image looks viewed through heat, water or clear jelly — contours drift and churn continuously; more turbulence layers and feedback produce more broken, rough liquefaction
continuum-bcc-twirl: Spins pixels into a spiral around a specified center — Linear, Wide, Narrow or opposing Two Way forms, with Twirl Angle, Radius, Inset, inner/outer Falloff and Aspect controlling strength, range and elliptical proportions.
Local footage swirls into a vortex or tornado with wider or narrower spirals in the center and outer ring; Two Way twists inside and outside the radius in opposite directions
continuum-bcc-wave: Parallel traveling waves across the whole source — Height and Perpendicular Height control displacement along and across the wave direction, Wave Width the crest spacing, Speed and Phase the crest movement direction, velocity and start position.
The frame undulates in rows like a flag, curtain or underwater image — parallel crests sweep across the material; shorter Wave Width adds dense fine ripples, negative Speed reverses the travel
gumroad-island-chatter: Synthesizes reproducible game-style character voices in Chinese, Japanese, and English in real time using native effects on text layers; a panel imports per-role scripts in batches, places lines by beat, connects lip-sync rigs or MIDI melodies, and bakes audio. For character dialogue, pixel-game narration, and lyric animations.
gumroad-zoom: A dockable panel that zooms the composition viewer to any scale via numeric input, dragging, and sliders; an optional helper plugin adds Ctrl/Cmd plus wheel and custom key bindings that keep the zoom centered on the cursor. For inspecting details and quickly navigating large frames.
gumroad-ez3d: Converts selected 2D layers to 3D, creates a parent Null for each, then staggers them along the Z axis with scale compensation to preserve the original composition; can also align to a shared depth plane or revert. For photo layering, depth push-ins, and 2.5D scenes.
gumroad-dither-fx-pro: One-click JSXBIN script that wraps selected layers into a reusable native-AE dithering rig with adjustable controls for reuse across different shots; no third-party plugins needed. For retro games, pixelated music visuals, and tech glitch shorts.
An adjustable low-bit dither and pixel grain built entirely from native AE effects.
gumroad-timeoffset: Offsets layers and keyframes inward or outward around the time cursor, including nested pre-comps; the newer version preserves protected zones and adjusts layer durations via time-stretch. For client length changes, inserting segments, and overall rhythm revisions.
gumroad-project-info-list-exporter: Takes stock of comps, layers, effects, missing plugins, asset paths, expressions, masks and Render Queue data in an After Effects project as a searchable, sortable list, with asset organization and cleanup tools; suited to handoffs, debugging and auditing large projects.
gumroad-rafikit-toolbox: Concentrates layer creation, precomp and un-precomp, project organization, cache cleanup, SRT subtitle import, text animation, common effects, bounce expressions and easing into a four-tab ScriptUI panel; suited to shortening repeated motion design work.
gumroad-letterblack-gen-ai: Generates animation, effects and expressions by chatting with OpenAI, Claude or Gemini in a CEP extension for After Effects 2025+, previewing live before applying, with batch processing for layers/comps and script error repair; suited to accelerating iterative motion design automation.
gumroad-vhs-emulator-for-ae-and-premiere: Applies VHS simulation to footage, text or logos in one click through the VHSfx extension for Adobe AE 2024/2025+, giving a drag-and-drop analog-tape retro look; suited to nostalgic openings, social captions and old-TV-style comps.
gumroad-field-driver-for-after-effects: Batch-drives layer position, scale, opacity, rotation, color, time remap and effect parameters through the distance relationship of a Null or path Field Controller, with elasticity, randomization and keyframe baking; suited to interactive motion design for UI, HUD, grids and many layers.
gumroad-ui-animator-pro: Builds editable keyframe or expression animation for UI interfaces with customizable presets, layer sequencing and one-click automation, importing HTML/Figma layouts, detecting UI screenshots into layers and auto-adding matching sound effects; suited to app, website and SaaS product demo animation.
gumroad-3d-to-2d: Converts 3D layers under camera motion into visually equivalent 2D Position, Scale and Rotation, optionally baking compact keyframes or keeping live expression links, plus Corner Pin for perspective rotation; suited to flattening 3D comps for delivery or further editing.
gumroad-mgfx-v2-0: Collects, organizes and relinks project assets by custom multi-level folder structure, file extensions and AE label colors, with destination selection, cut/paste, saved settings and automatic cleanup; suited to archiving, handoffs and delivering large After Effects projects.
gumroad-diis: Quickly applies reusable styles and generates extra shading layers with a pixel compositing workflow in Adobe AE 2024+, following existing animation without frame-by-frame drawing, masking or tracking; suited to NPR characters, illustration and hand-drawn-feel animation.
gumroad-easecurve-for-after-effects: Edits segmentable Bezier easing with live preview in Adobe AE 2020+, baking Position overshoot, plus shape path looping, nine-point anchor repositioning and adjustable spring expressions; suited to unifying keyframe rhythm and looping animation.
gumroad-docharts: Builds customizable bar charts from a dockable JSXBIN panel, with twenty-plus controls for position, spacing, size, color, animation and stagger timing; suited to infographics, presentation data and animated statistics.
gumroad-superselect-for-after-effects: Selects the same property or value across selected layers, same-parent layers or the whole comp from a JSXBIN panel or KBar and reveals it in the Timeline; suited to synchronized edits and animation across many layers.
gumroad-find-and-replace-in-expressions: Finds and batch-replaces specified text in After Effects expressions from a dockable window, suited to changing property references, variables, naming conventions or refactoring many existing expressions without opening layers one by one.
gumroad-pathprep-for-after-effects: Batch-converts parametric shapes such as rectangles, ellipses and polystars into editable Bezier Paths from a dockable JSXBIN panel, optionally baking Anchor/Position/Scale/Rotation into paths, selecting all paths or copying clean vector data; suited to preparing many shape layers for Illustrator, advanced path animation or point-by-point editing.
No fixed on-screen style is added; the shapes may look unchanged, but underneath they become baked, point-editable, copyable vector paths.
gumroad-keyframe-ai-image-generator-for-: Extracts single frames from the comp timeline via a ScriptUI panel, sends them to Replicate models such as Kontext, Nano Banana, Qwen Edit, Flux Fill or Seedream for reference-guided edits and mask inpainting, then auto-imports and orders the images; suited to video style frames, frame-by-frame VFX concepts and consistent source frames for AI video tools.
Frames can be repainted by reference image, restyled or mask-inpainted, then come back as an organized image sequence kept for re-compositing.
gumroad-post-notes-2: Creates rich-text notes and checkable to-dos inside each comp via a ZXP extension, with data embedded in the AEP so it travels with the project for other users to view and edit; suited to edit notes, client feedback and cross-team production lists.
No visual effect is produced; each comp can carry formatted notes and completable to-dos that are saved and shared with the AEP.
gumroad-code-buddy-ez-after-effects-expr: Saves, names, edits and applies your personal frequently used expressions from a dockable ScriptUI panel, applying them to the current property from a sorted list or clearing the expression on selected properties in one click; suited to building a long-term personal library of controllers, animation and layout expressions.
No fixed visual effect; the panel manages saved expressions as a selectable list and writes or clears them on the selected property in one click.
gumroad-render-markers: Reads markers in the active comp, adding durationless markers to the Render Queue as single-frame exports and duration markers as complete video segments; suited to creating precise batch renders for review points, chapters or delivery ranges without resetting the Work Area each time.
No image treatment is added; marker positions become single-frame or duration-based Render Queue jobs, letting one comp deliver multiple stills and segments in a batch.
gumroad-machine-vision: Analyzes selected footage layers and automatically generates a machine-vision overlay of boxes, nodes, links and data labels, with controls for sample density, sensitivity, node shape, color, blend mode and coordinate, angle or confidence readouts; suited to sci-fi HUDs, sports analysis, forensic interfaces and product-data visuals.
Boxes, circular or diamond nodes and connecting lines distribute over the footage, with diagnostic HUD readouts such as coordinates, timecode, color and visual-confidence scores.
gumroad-beatflow: Analyzes selected audio layers in After Effects: Music mode detects beats and directly creates comp markers, while Voice mode trims silence, keeps or removes gaps and creates phrase markers before automatically cutting layers by audio markers; suited to rhythm editing, interview tightening and voiceover-led motion design.
gumroad-forma: Loads OBJ 3D models as a native After Effects effect and renders anti-aliased wireframes or filled faces, with mesh position, rotation, scale, perspective, orthographic or isometric projection and pivot controls; it can also build XYZ model arrays, show vertex normals, and control the background and backface culling for product diagrams, technical graphics, abstract meshes and data visuals.
Imported 3D models appear as clean, controllable wireframes or flat filled faces, repeatable as spatial arrays and viewable in perspective, orthographic or isometric projections.
gumroad-pinrig: Builds controllable composition rigs for logos, typography and vector art in After Effects, automatically creating pins, Bézier handles, selection bounds, bounding boxes, corner radii, edge lengths, vertex coordinates and angle guides; it can save groups of pins, measurements and Null styles as reusable workflows for brand identity, logo builds and technical-diagram animation.
Animated pins, tangents, grids, dimension lines and coordinate marks surround the logo or text, creating precise brand-construction and drafting guides.
gumroad-rigtrect: Uses two controllers to build native AE expression rigs: RigtRect generates an animatable Shape Layer rectangle between two points, RigtSource stretches a source layer between them, and RigtFill preserves content proportions while filling the range in the same rig; it supports anchor placement, broken-rig repair and selection-based workflows for responsive layouts and deliverable MOGRTs.
When the two controllers move, rectangles, text or images automatically extend, scale or proportionally fill between them, forming flexible caption frames and layout components.
gumroad-ae-linguine: Switches the After Effects interface among English, Spanish and French from a ScriptUI panel, using Debug Database preferences instead of manually renaming system folders; it also provides a floating license that transfers automatically between computers, for editors and motion designers who follow foreign-language tutorials or work across language environments.
installed-topaz-video-ai: AI video restoration and enhancement engine: upscales low-resolution footage to 4K/8K, removes noise and compression artifacts, deinterlaces, and uses optical-flow frame interpolation for slow motion and higher frame rates. The go-to for restoring old footage and rescuing phone-camera quality.
installed-fast-camera-lens-blur: GPU-accelerated, high-quality lens bokeh and depth-of-field blur with customizable aperture-blade shapes, highlight bloom, and chromatic aberration; more realistic bokeh than AE's built-in. For shallow depth of field and blurred backgrounds.
installed-crate-s-godrays: Free: fast, beautiful volumetric light / radial rays. Click to set the light source, then adjust ray length, exposure, falloff, and chromatic aberration. Works from natural god rays to searchlights and holographic beams.
installed-physarum: Simulates the organic growth network of slime mold (physarum) foraging: many particles self-organize into mycelium / blood-vessel / neural patterns based on sensing angles and trail decay, and can interact with layers. For organic abstract backgrounds and growth animations.
installed-scaleup: AI neural-network upscaler that enlarges footage and enhances quality while suppressing noise and compression artifacts, beating traditional bilinear / bicubic interpolation. Sharp mode preserves detail; Cartoon mode suits animation line art.
installed-soft-body: Soft-body (jelly) dynamics in AE: the Quick engine adds automatic jiggle with one click, while the Advance engine handles detailed soft-body deformation and collisions. Supports shapes, text, and pre-comps with multiple colliders.
installed-furikake: Lightweight, high-performance particle plugin that uses multi-core CPUs fully to handle huge particle counts smoothly; supports multi-frame rendering, depth of field, and 32-bit color. For quick sprinkling / floating particles and fine decorative particles.
installed-retrodither: GPU dithering stylization that redraws the image with the hardware palettes of retro computers and game consoles (Commodore 64, Apple II, CGA, ZX Spectrum) for an authentic retro pixel look.
installed-motion-mosh: Real-time datamosh-style glitch: hijacks the image's motion vectors to produce trails and pixel displacement, without the usual export-then-reimport workflow; adjusts interactively right in AE / Pr.
installed-pixel-galactic: GPU effect that turns image motion into dreamy trails, glitch echoes, and flowing pixel distortion; for beautiful afterimages, psychedelic flow, and light glitch.
installed-gaussian-splatting: Real-time GPU import, manipulation, and rendering of 3D Gaussian splatting (.ply) real-world scans in AE: spherical / box clipping, compositing up to 10 models, gradient coloring, fade-in by opacity, and depth-pass output for 3D compositing. Generate splats with PostShot, Scaniverse, etc., then import.
installed-normal-mapper: GPU-accelerated conversion of any raster asset's luma into a normal map; adjust details first with AE blur, noise, or high-contrast effects, then export to 3D software or engines.
installed-live2d-cubism-for-ae: Loads Cubism models and motion files directly in AE and animates the character; ideal for VTuber illustrations, character introductions, and 2D character compositing.
A layered illustration character can play expressions, poses, and motions right in the composition.
